articles.title: Davidovich no se recupera de la espalda y también se borra del US Open
articles.standfirst: El malagueño se había visto obligado a ausentarse de Estoril y los Masters 1000 de Montreal y Cincinnati
articles.summary: El malagueño se había visto obligado a ausentarse de Estoril y los Masters 1000 de Montreal y Cincinnati
articles.body: Alejandro Davidovich, número 27 del ranking ATP a sus 27 años, no se ha recuperado a tiempo de la dolencia en la espalda que le mantiene sin competir desde su participación en el Open 250 de Umag. Lo ha intentado en las últimas sesiones realizadas estos días en Montecarlo, donde tiene fijada su residencia, pero no está en condiciones de disputar duelos a cinco sets. Es por ello que el malagueño se ha borrado este jueves de la lista de inscritos del US Open (30 de agosto al 13 de septiembre). La última vez que Davidovich se vistió de corto fue en los cuartos de Umag, sobre tierra batida, con Alex Molcan. Desde entonces, renunció a Estoril y los dos Masters 1000 de la gira americana de pista dura: Montreal y Cincinnati.  Tampoco pudo entrar en la convocatoria del equipo español de la Copa Davis que se medirá los días 19 y 20 de septiembre a Chile en Santiago. David Ferrer, el seleccionador nacional, le tenía en sus planes.    Álex, que estará más de un mes y medio de baja deportiva, intentará estar en condiciones de reaparecer en el Open 250 de Chengdu (23 al 29 de septiembre), la siguiente parada en su calendario ya en la gira asiática. Después está apuntado a Tokio antes del Masters 1000 de Shanghái.  En el Abierto de los Estados Unidos, donde iba a ser uno de los 32 cabezas de serie, restará los 50 puntos de la segunda ronda de la pasada edición. Tanta inactividad podría alejarle del 'top30' a la conclusión del grande neoyorquino.  El tenis español sigue pendiente de las evoluciones de Carlos Alcaraz, número tres mundial y que sigue siendo duda en el US Open por la lesión en la muñeca que no le ha dejado competir desde el 14 de abril. Alcaraz está entrenando toda esta semana en Murcia con Holger Rune de improvisado 'sparring'.

articles.title: Cristina Bucsa completa el quinteto español de la Billie Jean King Cup
articles.standfirst: España empezará su andadura con la Kazajistán de Elena Rybakina
articles.summary: España empezará su andadura con la Kazajistán de Elena Rybakina
articles.body: La selección nacional de la Billie Jean King Cup ha completado su alineación para la fase final de la máxima competición por países que se celebrará en Shenzhen (22 al 27 de septiembre) con la presencia de Cristina Bucsa, la 38 del ranking a sus 28 años. La tenista de Torrelavega, que ahora mismo es la número uno del tenis femenino español, se une a los nombres de Jessica Bouzas, Kaitlin Quevedo, Marina Bassols y Sara Sorribes.  España debutará en el torneo el próximo 23 de septiembre, en la ronda de cuartos, contra la Kazajistán de Elena Rybakina. Esta podría llegar a la cita como nueva número uno mundial después del nuevo traspié de Aryna Sabalenka en Cincinnati ante Sara Bejlek.  A Rybakina le vale con alcanzar la final en el torneo de Ohio para superar a Sabalenka en la clasificación mundial.

articles.title: Novak Djokovic documentary: Tennis great on being 'my own biggest doubter' and childhood that shaped his career
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic discusses being his own biggest doubter and the Belgrade childhood that shaped him in a new documentary.
articles.body:
Nobody doubts Novak Djokovic more than himself.

Djokovic has won almost everything there is in tennis. No man has more Grand Slam singles titles or Masters 1,000 crowns than him. He will go down in history as one of the greatest players of all time, if not the greatest.

But even now, at the age of 39, that is not enough for the Serb.

"I cannot say I feel content with what I have and who I am," he says in a new Amazon documentary.

"I am always looking to be more - better, faster, stronger. Oftentimes I feel I am imprisoning myself."

He says later in the documentary: "I'm the number one doubter. I'm trying to prove myself wrong more than anybody else."

Djokovic is level with Margaret Court for the most Grand Slam singles titles in history, having won his 24th trophy at the 2023 US Open.

He has reached at least the semi-finals at six of the past seven Grand Slams and in January became the oldest man in history to reach the Australian Open final.

"He definitely has mixed feelings about his retirement," his wife, Jelena, says.

"'He carries that burden that he's never enough. No matter how much he does, it will never be enough.

"Tennis is a fulfilling place for him - a place where he feels worthy."

The documentary shows footage of a young Djokovic being interviewed on television. Asked how he feels about tennis, he calls it a "responsibility".

"My goal in tennis is to become a champion," he says.

Djokovic's career, from his style of play to his attitude on court, has been shaped by his childhood experiences in a way that few other players can possibly relate.

Born in Belgrade, Djokovic was a young child during the Nato bombings of the Serbian capital between March and June 1999.

He recalls running from his building - which did not have a bomb shelter - to another for safety. On the way, he tripped, and his unaware family continued running. Djokovic turned to look at his building and watched a plane drop two bombs on a nearby hospital.

"Pretty much every day, for years, we had to wait in line for bread and milk," Djokovic told BBC 5 Live in July.

"These are defining moments, something I want to portray as a building block for me as a player and a person.

"There is no regret or resentment. In contrary, it's appreciation and gratitude. Everything in life happens as a reason."

In an expensive and often elitist sport, the young Djokovic was an outsider. Djokovic speaks about his father borrowing money from "wrong people" to fund his early tennis career.

When he broke through, he disrupted the Roger Federer-Rafael Nadal rivalry that had come to engross fans. More emotive and more vocal than the pair on court, Djokovic was not universally beloved by fans.

"I had to suppress a lot of emotions which, later on, surfaced on the court," he told BBC 5 Live.

"On the court, that's where I felt safe and comfortable. It was a familiar ground.

"Tennis is much more than a game and competition. It is defining ground for who I am as a person."

'I don't have expiry date for my career'

Every Djokovic loss at a Grand Slam is followed by questions about his retirement. However his 2026 US Open campaign pans out, Djokovic will be ready for familiar talk about his future in tennis.

Long-time rivals Federer and Nadal ended their careers in 2022 and 2024 respectively, having struggled with injuries in their latter years.

Djokovic has limited his schedule in recent years, playing very few tournaments outside of the Grand Slams.

After losing to Sinner at Wimbledon last year, Djokovic said he was competing at the latter stages of Slams with the "tank half-empty".

However, Djokovic says he does not have "the expiry date of my career" in mind.

"Why would I talk about retirement when I still keep proving to myself that I can still win?" he says in the documentary.

"As long as I have the drive, the passion, but most of all, as long as I feel like I can be one of the best players in the world, I want to keep going."

Winning a long-awaited Olympic gold medal in Paris in 2024 was the pinnacle of Djokovic's career, and he is still aiming for the 2028 Games in Los Angeles.

"It seems a long way out. I feel like I can make it," he added.

"I would like to end with the Serbian flag on my shoulders.

"It would be a nice way to wrap up something I'm very proud of."

Djokovic has won almost everything there is in tennis. No man has more Grand Slam singles titles or Masters 1,000 crowns than him. He will go down in history as one of the greatest players of all time, if not the greatest.
But even now, at the age of 39, that is not enough for the Serb.
"I cannot say I feel content with what I have and who I am," he says in a new Amazon documentary.
"I am always looking to be more - better, faster, stronger. Oftentimes I feel I am imprisoning myself."
He says later in the documentary: "I'm the number one doubter. I'm trying to prove myself wrong more than anybody else."
Djokovic is level with Margaret Court for the most Grand Slam singles titles in history, having won his 24th trophy at the 2023 US Open.
He has reached at least the semi-finals at six of the past seven Grand Slams and in January became the oldest man in history to reach the Australian Open final.
"He definitely has mixed feelings about his retirement," his wife, Jelena, says.
"'He carries that burden that he's never enough. No matter how much he does, it will never be enough.
"Tennis is a fulfilling place for him - a place where he feels worthy."

articles.title: US Open Announces Historic $108M Purse, Full Prize Money Breakdown Revealed for Tennis Grand Slam
articles.summary: There is going to be a record-setting amount of money on the line for the 2026 U.S. Open tennis tournament.
articles.body:
There is going to be a record-setting amount of money on the line for the 2026 U.S. Open tennis tournament.

As Lev Akabas of Sportico relayed Thursday, the prize money for the Grand Slam event is up 20 percent from last year's edition. The 2025 total was already a record-setting one, and the 2026 tournament will feature even more at stake with a $108 million total purse and $5.5 million for the singles winners.

Even the first-round losers will take home $140,000.

The Associated Press provided a further breakdown, noting quarterfinalists will make $780,000, semifinalists will make $1.45 million and runners-up will make $2.8 million.

It represents a head-turning 44 percent jump since 2024.

Thursday's announcement comes as the financials of the tennis world were under something of a spotlight. Matthew Futterman of The Athletic reported such an increase in the purse "has likely staved off the player protests over remuneration that took place at this year's editions of the French Open and Wimbledon."

Futterman noted the U.S. Tennis Association committed to three requests from the players of welfare contributions, a Grand Slam player council and prize-money tied to revenues.

All four Grand Slams also announced the creation of the player council.

"Having a seat at the table with the Grand Slams is something we have wanted for some time, so I'm really pleased to see this council come together," Ben Shelton said. "It gives us, as players, a real opportunity to have a voice, contribute to the conversation and help shape the tournaments beyond what happens on the court."

Players will have the ability to raise compensation concerns through the council.

"This is a significant first step in a multi-year investment in athletes as the U.S. Open continues to be the best economic opportunity for players and the most valuable platform in tennis for players, fans and partners," USTA leader Craig Tiley said. "We are proud to deliver record-setting prize money and expanded player benefits as well as providing a new platform to work together with players."

This year's U.S. Open starts on Sunday, Aug. 23 and runs through the men's single final on Sunday, Sept. 13.

Carlos Alcaraz is the reigning champion on the men's side and took home the coveted trophy in two of the last four years. Aryna Sabalenka is the back-to-back champion on the women's side and also reached the 2023 final, where she lost to Coco Gauff.

One of the biggest questions for this year's tournament is whether Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner will play and be effective after facing each other in last year's final.

They each withdrew from this month's Masters 1000 tournament in Cincinnati with injury concerns, and there remains uncertainty if they will both be able to take the court in New York.

articles.title: Nace el Consejo Asesor de Jugadores para negociar con los Grand Slam
articles.standfirst: Los torneos de mayor categoría del tenis anuncian un Consejo Asesor de Jugadores
articles.summary: Los torneos de mayor categoría del tenis anuncian un Consejo Asesor de Jugadores
articles.body: Australian Open, Roland Garros, Wimbledon y US Open, han anunciado la creación de un Consejo Asesor de Jugadores aprobado por los cuatro torneos de Grand Slam que se pondrá en marcha tras la finalización del US Open 2026. Ante la lluvia de críticas de ambos circuitos (ATP y WTA), mayormente impulsadas por el "bajo premio económico" que repartían los cuatro 'majors', las organizaciones de los torneos de mayor categoría del mundo del tenis han formado un consejo para favorecer la comunicación y colaboración entre los jugadores y los propios Grand Slam.  "El Consejo proporcionará una nueva plataforma para que los jugadores y los Grand Slam trabajen juntos para dar forma al futuro de los torneos y avanzar en nuestro objetivo compartido de un mayor apoyo a los jugadores", es el mensaje que han publicado los cuatro certámenes en sus redes sociales. Los máximos exponentes del tenis americano, Ben Shelton y Jessica Pegula, han aplaudido la iniciativa: "Tener voz y voto en los Grand Slam es algo que deseábamos desde hace tiempo, así que me alegra mucho ver que este consejo se haya formado. Nos brinda, como jugadores, una oportunidad real de expresar nuestra opinión, contribuir al diálogo y ayudar a dar forma a los torneos más allá de lo que sucede en la pista”, fueron las palabras del número seis del mundo. La tercera espada del ranking WTA, Jessica Pegula, también ha querido compartir su perspectiva: "Los Grand Slam son los eventos más importantes del año. Su impacto en la carrera de un jugador es incalculable, y por eso es tan importante que tengamos voz en estos torneos. La formación de este consejo de jugadores representa precisamente eso, y me complace que los Grand Slam lo hayan llevado a cabo”. Deborah Jevans, presidenta del All England Club, declaró haber escuchado el deseo de los jugadores: "Hemos escuchado las peticiones de los jugadores de tener mayor voz y este consejo asesor es un paso importante hacia una relación más sólida entre los Grand Slam y los propios tenistas". "Esperamos trabajar juntos para mejorar la experiencia de los jugadores, potenciar aún más los torneos de Grand Slam y garantizar que el deporte siga prosperando", añadió una de las máximas voces de los cuatro grandes.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz recrea las condiciones del US Open en sus entrenamientos en Murcia
articles.standfirst: El murciano ha aumentado las cargas de tiempo en las sesiones pasando de dos a tres y cuatro horas
articles.summary: El murciano ha aumentado las cargas de tiempo en las sesiones pasando de dos a tres y cuatro horas
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz y su equipo quieren estar seguros de que los siguientes pasos, por lo que hace referencia a la conveniencia de volver a jugar, sean los correctos. En la semana previa al inicio del Abierto de los Estados Unidos (30 de agosto al 13 de septiembre), el campeón de siete grandes recrea en su Murcia natal la intensidad y las condiciones (se han llegado a los 40 grados) que se podría encontrar en las pistas de Flushing Meadows.  Si finalmente decide viajar a Nueva York, tendrá que hacerlo a principios de la semana que viene. Es por ello que la decisión sobre su participación en el último grande es inminente.  Tal y como relata Germán Abril, Alcaraz ha pasado de realizar sesiones de dos horas a practicar durante tres e incluso cuatro horas. Ha sido el caso de la práctica de este jueves. Toda la semana le está acompañando Holger Rune.  Cabe recordar que el joven de El Palmar, que el pasado 5 de mayo cumplió 23 años, es el vigente campeón del grande neoyorquino por lo que debe defender los 2.000 puntos de vencedor.

articles.title: Alcaraz ya está sano de la muñeca: regresa a las pistas en el US Open 138 días después
articles.standfirst: Carlitos se siente en condiciones de disputar el último grande tras las pruebas en pista realizadas esta semana en Murcia
articles.summary: Carlitos se siente en condiciones de disputar el último grande tras las pruebas en pista realizadas esta semana en Murcia
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, número dos mundial a sus 23 años, ve la luz al final del túnel. Después de una inactividad que se habrá alargado durante 138 días, el campeón de siete grandes está recuperado de la lesión en su muñeca derecha que se produjo el pasado 14 de abril en la primera ronda del Barcelona Open Banc Sabadell con Otto Virtanen.  Alcaraz, que tenía como objetivo inicial regresar el 13 de agosto en el Masters 1000 de Cincinnati, decidió quedarse en España y seguir entrenando. Era precipitado emprender la aventura americana sin poder pegarle a la pelota con plenas garantías.  El tenista añadió una malla compresora a su brazo derecho para sentirse más seguro en el golpeo. No era la primera vez que se decantaba por esa solución. En la primavera de 2024 también lució la malla en la gira de tierra batida después de lesionarse el antebrazo en su primer entrenamiento en Montecarlo.  La prueba de fuego la ha tenido esta semana recreando las condiciones del Abierto de los Estados Unidos durante las sesiones con Holger Rune, que se han llegado a alargar por espacio de cuatro horas. Este jueves ha sido el test definitivo que ha convencido a Carlitos y a su equipo de que está apto para volver a la competición oficial. Esta misma tarde, hizo oficial su vuelta a través de sus redes sociales con un mensaje contundente: 'Here we go' (allá vamos).  Alcaraz viajará a Nueva York este fin de semana para empezar desde ya mismo a realizar entrenamientos de máximo nivel con el resto de participantes al último grande. Falta saber si se apuntará al dobles mixto. La organización, con Craig Tiley a la cabeza, le guarda una de las tres invitaciones restantes.  El tenista de El Palmar podrá optar así a retener la corona de campeón, que son 2.000 puntos. Durante su ausencia se ha dejado sin defender un total de 6.130 puntos. Jannik Sinner, su gran rival, sigue siendo duda por sus molestias en la rodilla.  Alcaraz, que se borró en los octavos del Godó y se perdió después el Mutua Madrid Open, Roma, Roland Garros, Queen's, Wimbledon, Montreal y Cincinnati, jugará un total de siete torneos hasta final de temporada. Su regreso oficial será en el US Open (30 de agosto al 13 de septiembre); Después estará en la Laver Cup (25 al 27); Tokio (30 de septiembre al 6 de octubre); Shanghái (7 al 18 de octubre); Six Kings Slam (21 al 24 de octubre); París (2 al 8 de noviembre) y las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre). A su hoja de ruta añadiría las Finales de la Copa Davis de Bolonia si España vence a Chile a domicilio los días 19 y 20 de septiembre.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz to Return from Injury for 2026 US Open After Missing Wimbledon, Roland-Garros
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz confirmed Thursday that he will return from a wrist injury to play in the 2026 U.S. Open.
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz confirmed Thursday that he will return from a wrist injury to play in the 2026 U.S. Open.

Alcaraz made his return official in a joint Instagram post with world football insider Fabrizio Romano. "Here we go! Carlos Alcaraz will return to the tour at the U.S. Open after spending four months sidelined with a right wrist injury," Romano wrote.

Agassi, Serena and more iconic US Open outfits

The 23-year-old Alcaraz took to X to share the news as well on the heels of missing both the French Open and Wimbledon:

A seven-time Grand Slam singles champion, Alcaraz last played in the Barcelona Open back in April.

Alcaraz withdrew from the tournament due to a wrist injury after winning his first-round matchup, and that led to a prolonged absence that saw him miss both Roland-Garros in May and June, and Wimbledon in June and July.

The only Grand Slam tournament Alcaraz has played thus far in 2026 is the Australian Open. The Spaniard was victorious, allowing him to complete the career Grand Slam by winning all four major tournaments.

articles.title: Serena espera a Alcaraz en Nueva York para jugar un dobles mixto para la historia: "Me gusta ver que vienes"
articles.standfirst: El murciano parte este fin de semana hacia Nueva York y preparará a conciencia el US Open en Flushing Meadows
articles.summary: El murciano parte este fin de semana hacia Nueva York y preparará a conciencia el US Open en Flushing Meadows
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz y su equipo, con su entrenador Samuel López a la cabeza, parten este fin de semana hacia Nueva York. Allí les espera Serena Williams con los brazos abiertos. Y es que el próximo martes 25 de agosto puede hacerse realidad uno de los sueños de los aficionados al tenis. Alcaraz se juntaría con Serena para disputar un histórico dobles mixto.  "Me alegra de que vuelvas", escribió la leyenda estadounidense en redes sociales como respuesta al retorno oficial de Carlitos. El tenista de El Palmar le respondió con un reloj de arena. Iniciando así una cuenta para juntarse en mitad de pista. El campeón de siete grandes jugó el pasado mixto del Abierto de los Estados Unidos al lado de Emma Raducanu. Cedieron en el debut. Craig Tilley, nuevo mandamás del último grande y que llega procedente del Open de Australia, tiene reservada una invitación para Carlitos y Serena. Es consciente que el dúo llenará las gradas de la Arthur Ashe, con capacidad para 23.000 personas, la semana previa al inicio de la competición individual. Entre los participantes destacan la pareja formada por Novak Djokovic y Aryna Sabalenka.  La campeona de 23 grandes, madre de dos hijas y que regresó al circuito en el pasado Wimbledon, con derrota a la primera, tiene que decidir si acepta una 'wild card' para el individual en el Abierto de los Estados Unidos. Cabe recordar que el próximo 26 de septiembre cumplirá 45 años.

articles.title: Cincinnati Open: Iga Swiatek to face Jessica Pegula in semi-finals after Elena Rybakina suffers injury
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina took a medical timeout and then had to retire injured in the first set of her quarter-final against Iga Swiatek; Watch the US Open from August 30 live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Elena Rybakina was forced to retire from her quarter-final against Iga Swiatek at the Cincinnati Open due to an ankle injury.

The No 2-ranked Rybakina was trailing 4-1 when she took a medical timeout to have trainers address her left ankle and retired from the match moments later.

With top seed Aryna Sabalenka losing to Sara Bejlek, the 27-year-old Rybakina could have risen to No 1 in the rankings by reaching the final.

  • Alcaraz to make his return at US Open
  • Latest tennis scores and results 🎾
  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract 📱

Swiatek, the defending champion, has reached at least the semi-finals in each of her last four appearances in Cincinnati.

"Not the way you want the match to end," Swiatek said. "She didn't look good, obviously. Then she wanted treatment and I wasn't sure if she was going to be back or not.

"She is walking normally now. I felt really sorry for her but hopefully it's nothing serious and she is going to be ready for the US Open."

Swiatek beat Rybakina in the semi-finals in Cincinnati last year but this time will face American Jessica Pegula in the last four.

World No 3 Pegula came through a fightback from Amanda Anisimova to claim a ‌6-4 2-6 7-6(4) victory.

In the men's draw, seventh seed Flavio Cobolli made up for a poor start to beat American ​Tommy Paul 2-6 6-3 6-4 and reach his first ATP Masters ‌1000 semi-final.

He will play Arthur Fils for a place in the final after he defeated Argentina's Thiago Agustin Tirante 6-3 6-2.

articles.title: Rafa Jódar, el mejor a los 50 partidos
articles.standfirst: El madrileño mejora las cifras del 'Big Three', Alcaraz y Sinner, con un balance de 36 victorias y 14 derrotas
articles.summary: El madrileño mejora las cifras del 'Big Three', Alcaraz y Sinner, con un balance de 36 victorias y 14 derrotas
articles.body: A pesar de la eliminación en los octavos de Cincinnati a manos de Flavio Cobolli, Rafa Jódar mejora las estadísticas de los más grandes en su primera temporada como profesional. El joven madrileño, de tan sólo 19 años, presenta el mejor balance en la Era Open después de haber disputado sus primeros 50 partidos oficiales (no se cuentan los dos triunfos de las Next Gen Finals). Rafa cuenta con un balance de 36 victorias por 14 derrotas, el mismo registro que en su día firmó el argentino José Luis Clerc. La nueva sensación del tenis mundial mejora las cifras de Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner y el Big Three al llegar al medio centenar de duelos en el circuito. Alcaraz y Rafael Nadal tenían 31 triunfos, por los 30 de Sinner y los 27 de Roger Federer y Novak Djokovic. Los que más cerca están de Jódar en esa estadística son John McEnroe, Andy Roddick, Andrei Medvedev y Guillermo Párez Roldán, con 34 partidos ganados. Rafa, que pagó ante Cobolli el cansancio de una gira americana que para él empezó el 27 de julio en Washington —alcanzó las semifinales—, tendrá un mínimo descanso antes de preparar el asalto al US Open (30 de agosto al 13 de septiembre). Su primera sesión preparatoria en Nueva York será el martes 25 de agosto. Acumula ya 64 partidos jugados en 2026, de los que 13 corresponden a la actual gira norteamericana de superficie dura.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner confirma su baja para el US Open: "Estoy muy triste y decepcionado"
articles.standfirst: El italiano ha comunicado en redes sociales que "aún necesito más tiempo para recuperarme de mi problema en la rodilla derecha"
articles.summary: El italiano ha comunicado en redes sociales que "aún necesito más tiempo para recuperarme de mi problema en la rodilla derecha"
articles.body: Jannik Sinner anunció este viernes que no disputará el próximo US Open por problemas físicos. El italiano, que pasó a principios de agosto varios exámenes médicos para dilucidar si llegaba en condiciones óptimas al último Grand Slam del año, ha confirmado que no estará en el cuadro individual del torneo de Nueva York. "Aunque he estado trabajando duro con mi equipo y mi personal médico, ahora hemos tenido que tomar la difícil decisión de que no podré competir en el US Open de este año", aseguró en sus redes sociales. Sinner, que no disputa ningún encuentro desde que se coronara ganador en Wimbledon por segundo año consecutivo, explicó que "hemos vuelto a la pista en Montecarlo durante los últimos días y nos hemos dado cuenta de que aún necesito más tiempo para recuperarme de mi problema en la rodilla derecha". El italiano ya se había dado de baja de los Masters 1000 de Montreal y Cincinnati. Su ausencia definitiva se produce un día después de que Carlos Alcaraz anunciara su regreso cuatro meses después. El español ha estado alejando de las pistas por una lesión en la muñeca derecha que sufrió en abril, durante el torneo Conde de Godó de Barcelona. El italiano se mostró apesadumbrado por su ausencia en el último Grand Slam de la temporada: "Obviamente estoy muy triste y decepcionado, ya que Nueva York ocupa un lugar especial en mi corazón. Estaba muy ilusionado con regresar y jugar en la electrizante atmósfera frente a los grandes aficionados allí".

articles.title: Swiatek "salva" el número 1 de Sabalenka de cara al US Open
articles.standfirst: La polaca ya está en semifinales de Cincinnati tras la retirada de una Rybakina que ya no podrá optar al número uno en Estados Unidos
articles.summary: La polaca ya está en semifinales de Cincinnati tras la retirada de una Rybakina que ya no podrá optar al número uno en Estados Unidos
articles.body: Iga Swiatek le ha hecho un "favor" a Aryna Sabalenka tras su clasificación a las semifinales del TMS de Ohio. La actual reina del circuito conservará su condición como número uno, al menos de cara al US Open ante la retirada de Elena Rybakina cuando perdía por 4-1 en el primer set. Un desenlace que pocos querían para el que tenía todas las papeletas de ser el mejor encuentro del torneo. Iga entró a la pista en modo máquina. Salvó una bola de 'break' en el juego inicial y acto seguido aprovechó su primera oportunidad para, no solo romper el saque, sino también todos los esquemas de la kazaja. El tremendo trabajo de pies de la polaca, clave en el inicio. En el sexto juego Rybakina decía adiós al partido y a sus opciones de ser número 1 (tenía que llegar a la final para conseguirlo). Notó molestias en su pierna izquierda en mitad de un intercambio, dolores que persistieron en el saque posterior y obligaron a la kazaja a abandonar cuando cedía por 4-1 en 28 minutos. La segunda raqueta mundial hace saltar todas las alarmas de cara al último grande del año que empieza en tan solo cuatro días (del 25 de agosto al 13 de septiembre). Debido a su pase a la penúltima ronda del certamen americano, Iga Swiatek ya es la tercera jugadora con más apariciones en semifinales de Masters 1000, firma 24. Siendo solo superada por Serena Williams (26) y Simona Halep (29). Tiempo al tiempo de que las supere. Se las verá con Jessica Pegula por un pase a la final. En el apartado masculino, el francés Arthur Fils acabó con la gran semana del argentino Tirante, verdugo de Djokovic, Landaluce y Mensik, y jugará sus terceras semifinales de Masters 1000 ante Flavio Cobolli. El italiano derrotó a Tommy Paul en tres mangas en los cuartos de final. En caso de que el diestro de Florencia venza en su duelo de semifinales, le arrebatará a Novak Djokovic el quinto puesto del ranking ATP y quedará virtualmente entre los cinco mejores.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner Out of 2026 US Open with Knee Injury, World No. 1 Explains Decision in Statement
articles.summary: Jannik Sinner has withdrawn from the 2026 U.S. Open due to a knee injury.
articles.body:
Jannik Sinner has withdrawn from the 2026 U.S. Open due to a knee injury.

The U.S. Open officially announced Sinner's withdrawal from the tournament and Carlos Taberner will be added to the main draw.

In a statement on X, Sinner explained the right knee injury that has kept him out since winning Wimbledon has yet not recovered to the point that he is ready to play in a full tournament.

Agassi, Serena and more iconic US Open outfits

Sinner withdrew from the Canadian Open that began on Aug. 2 due to what he described as "health reasons." He was also scheduled to take part in the Cincinnati Open, but wound up skipping the event to rest and recover.

The last time Sinner played was on July 12 when he defeated Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon gentlemen's final to win his second straight title at the All England Club.

Sinner, currently the No. 1 player in the ATP rankings, would have been the top seed at the U.S. Open when the draw is announced on Aug. 27.

Instead, the honor could go to Carlos Alcaraz in his return to competition. The 23-year-old announced on Thursday he will play in the U.S. Open after missing four months due to a wrist injury.

Alcaraz last played at the Barcelona Open when he had to withdraw prior to a second-round match against Tomáš Macháč. He is looking for his second Grand Slam tournament victory of the season after winning the Australian Open in February.

This will be the first major tournament Sinner hasn't played since the 2019 French Open when he was still playing primarily on the Challenger Tour.

Sinner reached the final at the U.S. Open in each of the previous two years. He won in 2024 by defeating Taylor Fritz, then lost to Alcaraz in four sets last year.

The 2026 U.S. Open begins on Aug. 30 and runs through Sept. 13.

The last time Sinner played was on July 12 when he defeated Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon gentlemen's final to win his second straight title at the All England Club.
Sinner, currently the No. 1 player in the ATP rankings, would have been the top seed at the U.S. Open when the draw is announced on Aug. 27.
Instead, the honor could go to Carlos Alcaraz in his return to competition. The 23-year-old announced on Thursday he will play in the U.S. Open after missing four months due to a wrist injury.

Alcaraz last played at the Barcelona Open when he had to withdraw prior to a second-round match against Tomáš Macháč. He is looking for his second Grand Slam tournament victory of the season after winning the Australian Open in February.
This will be the first major tournament Sinner hasn't played since the 2019 French Open when he was still playing primarily on the Challenger Tour.
Sinner reached the final at the U.S. Open in each of the previous two years. He won in 2024 by defeating Taylor Fritz, then lost to Alcaraz in four sets last year.
The 2026 U.S. Open begins on Aug. 30 and runs through Sept. 13.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner: World No 1 withdraws from US Open with knee injury and misses out on final Grand Slam of the season
articles.summary: 2024 US Open champion Jannik Sinner announces he will not be able to feature at Flushing Meadows; world No 1 has not played since winning Wimbledon in July; Sinner lost to Carlos Alcaraz in last year's final; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
World No 1 Jannik Sinner has withdrawn from this month's US Open due to a right knee injury.

Sinner has been out of action since winning Wimbledon last month, his fifth Grand Slam title, where he beat Alexander Zverev in the final to successfully defend his title at the All England Club.

He missed the Masters 1000 events in Canada and Cincinnati, pulling out of the latter with a right knee injury to focus on being ready to play at Flushing Meadows, but has confirmed he will be unable to feature in New York.

  • Latest tennis scores and results 🎾
  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract 📱

In a statement on social media, 2024 champion Sinner said: "Even though I have been working hard with my team and my medical staff, we have now had to make the difficult decision that I will not be able to compete at the US Open this year.

"We have been back on court in Monte Carlo over the last couple of days and have realised that I still need more time to recover from my right knee issue.

"I'm obviously very sad and disappointed, as New York has a special place in my heart. I was very much looking forward to coming back and playing in the electric atmosphere in front of the great fans there."

A 'shock' losing Sinner with Alcaraz to make comeback

Sinner's withdrawal comes a day after his great rival Carlos Alcaraz, who the Italian lost to in the final 12 months ago, revealed he will make his comeback from four months out with a wrist injury.

Spain's Carlos Taberner moves into the men's singles draw after Sinner's withdrawal, with Alcaraz now the highest-ranked player in action despite his recent injury troubles.

Alcaraz will be chasing his third US Open title, live on Sky Sports from August 30, having won his first Grand Slam title there in 2022 to reach world No 1 before lifting the trophy for a second time last September.

Speaking to Gigi Salmon on Sky Sports, former British No 1 Annabel Croft said: "It's quite a shock to be honest. We knew he hadn't played the last couple of events and he was resting but that whole idea was to get ready for the US Open.

"It's a big blow to tennis because it feels like a long time ago that we had Alcaraz and Sinner in the events together and it feels like a great loss."

Croft continued: "It also underlines how relentless and demanding the tour is physically. When you think at the beginning of the year when he won those five back-to-back Masters 1000 titles which was absolutely exceptional and a phenomenal achievement, but when he got to Roland-Garros there was not much left in the tank and it cost him perhaps the French Open title..

"Then we saw him rebound at Wimbledon which he built with each match but once again his body has let himself down. For all of these players it's such a difficult balance. You keep trying to play the tour, play the mandatory events but you also want to peak at the Grand Slams and it's not quite happening at the moment."

Former world No 40 Ryan Harrison added: "Sinner feels the risk of playing the US Open is a little bit too much."

Is the Tour being carried by Alcaraz and Sinner?

Croft said: "It's a long time since we had them in the same draw [since Monte Carlo]. They have become the new rivalry that everyone wants to see. I really don't mind watching the same players compete all the time because those are the matches you really look forward to.

"It's like watching a big boxing fight. You want to see the very best go up against each other, but now it's an opportunity for the next category down to shine. It's interesting because it's a bit of a transitional period at the moment.

"Who knows what will happen when we get them all back together."

Watch the ATP and WTA Tours live on Sky Sports. The US Open is also live on Sky Sports from August 30. Stream tennis with NOW.

articles.title: Jack Draper: British star ruled out of the US Open due to ongoing injury woes
articles.summary: Jack Draper follows Jannik Sinner out of the US Open in the latest blow to the former world No 4; watch the US Open from August 30 live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
British star Jack Draper has been ruled out of the US Open as he continues to battle a bone bruise in his dominant left arm.

After two dispiriting matches in the United States, Draper has concluded he needs more time to recover, according to sources close to the player.

The news, which came only a couple of hours after world No 1 Jannik Sinner announced he would miss the tournament with a knee injury, while Carlos Alcaraz is set to make his return after a four-month spell on the sidelines with a wrist injury.

  • Latest tennis scores and results 🎾
  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract 📱

The former world No 4, who has not played at a single Grand Slam this year, said he was in a "difficult place" after his first-round defeat by Martin Landaluce in the Cincinnati Open last week, admitting he was struggling to escape the mental fatigue that had built up during 15 months of battling serious injury.

Draper told the Guardian: "It's the same as last week, the way I'm usually able to fight for every ball and conduct myself, it's just missing.

"Obviously, the conditions and all the things that I'm changing is very hard to manage, but I think from just an internal point of view, it's a difficult place to be right now."

Draper has made a series of changes to reduce the strain on his left arm. Since Wimbledon, the 24-year-old has altered his strings and racket, while continuing to tweak his service motion.

He admitted managing it is a constant challenge, saying: "It's got to a point with me where it's taken probably one of my biggest qualities, my fighting spirit.

"There's a level of chronic pain that's always with you. When you've got that on your playing arm - this is my life, this is my career, you know?

"When you've got an injury that is tough to come past and tough to understand, there's many challenges, there's many obstacles."

Croft: Draper needs to try and fix his body!

Speaking to Gigi Salmon on Sky Sports Tennis, Annabel Croft said it was a bit of "doom and gloom" around tennis at the moment.

"Maybe we weren't so surprised," said the former British No 1. "We knew something was up when we saw that eruption of emotion just a couple of events ago. I got the impression this horrible long-term injury - the bone bruising in his arm just wasn't going away - it was rearing its ugly head again and he spoke quite openly about it.

"He's tried everything and it just keeps coming back, so maybe this is a good decision because to go into a Grand Slam, it's best of five sets and it's absolutely brutal.

"It's seven matches back-to-back and they've looked at that and decided he's not ready for that.

"He needs to go away and try - I don't know how - to fix his body. It's been so emotional for him because he wants to go out there and compete.

"The US Open is a Grand Slam where he has reached the semi-finals. He has challenged all of the very best in the world, so I feel very sad for him."

Draper's injury timeline after Wimbledon 2025...

  • July-Aug 2025: Break until the US Open
  • Aug 2025: US Open mixed doubles, then one singles match before withdrawing with a left-arm injury
  • Sep 2025-Jan 2026: Out injured
  • Feb 2026: Returned to competition
  • Apr 2026: Retired in Barcelona with a knee injury and was out for more than two months.
  • June 2026: Returned at Eastbourne; then withdrew from Wimbledon
  • Aug 2026: Returned at Montreal and Cincinnati
  • Aug 21, 2026: Withdrew from the US Open with his left-arm injury

What's happening to tennis? Has it become too long and relentless?

Former player turned coach, Ryan Harrison said: "It's 11 months and it's non-stop. The year-end championship comes along in November, which is such a big event with the prestige to try and finish world No 1. We saw a world No 1 race right to the very end last year between Sinner and Alcaraz. There's a lot of incentive there to try and get to that top spot but for me it's the way the courts are playing and the way the balls are playing now.

"It's not as friendly to big serving and it's not as friendly to points being quick anymore because the courts have slowed down, while the conditions have slowed down so we're seeing a lot more longer, physical rallies, and that's more physically demanding on the body.

"I think it's even more difficult to stay healthy now than it was say 20 or 30 years ago when the courts were more friendly to service winners and aces.

"Nowadays, the 11 months, the physicality, the demands of the tour. We love seeing these epic matches and epic rallies, but the body pays for that price."

Does change need to happen?

Croft said: "It's very difficult to change the calendar because so many of the tournaments are individually owned and you have all the sponsorship around that. It's difficult to take it away!

"It does feel the surfaces have all been coming together a lot more and there wasn't so much definition. I think a lot of the players would like to see a lot of the courts quickened up."

articles.title: Holger Rune decide no jugar el US Open tras la semana de entrenamientos con Alcaraz
articles.standfirst: El danés agradece al equipo del español la semana en Murcia y no regresará en el grande neoyorquino
articles.summary: El danés agradece al equipo del español la semana en Murcia y no regresará en el grande neoyorquino
articles.body: Holger Rune y Carlos Alcaraz han pasado una semana de entrenamientos juntos en la Real Sociedad Club de Campo de Murcia, ambos preparando su puesta a punto de cara a la vuelta al circuito. Cabe recordar que el danés lleva sin jugar desde el 18 de octubre de 2025 por una lesión en el tendón de Aquiles de su pierna izquierda. Finalmente, Rune ha decidido que lo mejor será no correr riesgos y saltarse el US Open para continuar con su preparación: "Mi equipo y yo hemos decidido no disputar un Grand Slam como mi primer torneo de regreso. US Open, nos vemos el próximo año", compartió el que fuera número cuatro del mundo en sus redes sociales abandonando la posibilidad de estar en Flushing Meadows. También agradeció a Carlos Alcaraz y su equipo por la semana de trabajo: "Gracias a Carlos Alcaraz y al equipo por la gran semana de entrenamientos en Murcia. Muy contento por mi avance y nivel. Seguimos trabajando", así cerraba el mensaje Holger que ya ve muy cerca su regreso a los torneos profesionales.

articles.title: Cincinnati Open: Coco Gauff races into semi-finals as USA eye titles in men's and women's tournaments
articles.summary: Coco Gauff reached her fifth WTA 1000 semi-final of 2026, as Frances Tiafoe and Brandon Nakashima lined up a last-four cracker in the men's tournament; Watch the US Open from August 30 live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Coco Gauff swept into the semi-finals of the Cincinnati Open with a 70-minute dismantling of Marta Kostyuk.

The 22-year-old's 6-2 6-2 win over the Ukrainian carried her into a fifth WTA 1000 semi-final of the year and a second in Cincinnati, where she lifted the title in 2023.

  • Alcaraz to make his return at US Open
  • Latest tennis scores and results 🎾
  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract 📱

Standing between Gauff and another final is the tournament's giant-killer.

Sara Bejlek, the unseeded 20-year-old who stunned world No 1 Aryna Sabalenka in straight sets in the last 16, came from a set down to beat 2019 champion Madison Keys 3-6 6-4 7-6 (7-5) and reach the first WTA 1000 semi-final of her career.

"Sara is a great player," Gauff said. "I watched her a lot in Abu Dhabi this year when she won that title. So I think it's going to be a tough match. I'm looking forward to it."

Bejlek, who won that Abu Dhabi Open title back in February when she was ranked outside the world's top 100, believes her mentality has improved now when facing the top echelon of players in the women's game.

"I believe in myself much more than I ever have before," said the rising Czech star.

World No 3 Jessica Pegula beat Amanda Anisimova in a third set tie-break on Thursday and faces world No 5 and defending champion Iga Swiatek in the other semi-final.

With two Americans also in the semis of the men's singles, Gauff is dreaming of a home sweep this week.

"It's insane, I think we're all doing so well," she said. "Hopefully we can have a double title win. Obviously there are more matches to be played for that to happen. We definitely root for each other."

Tiafoe and Nakashima book first all-US men's semi since 2010

In the men's draw, Frances Tiafoe and Brandon Nakashima made history of their own, becoming the first two Americans to reach the Cincinnati semi-finals since Andy Roddick and Mardy Fish in 2010.

Tiafoe, the 2024 runner-up to Jannik Sinner, needed more than two hours and four match points to see off 10th seed Lorenzo Musetti 7-6 (7-2) 7-5 on a humid Ohio night, firing 18 winners before sealing it with an unreturnable serve as he looks to revive a summer disrupted by a wrist injury and early exits in Washington and Montreal.

Nakashima recovered from a break down in the deciding set to beat sixth seed Taylor Fritz 7-6 (11-9) 4-6 6-3, a fourth top-10 win of the season that makes him the first American man to reach the semi-finals in Canada and Cincinnati in the same year since Mardy Fish in 2011.

Nakashima, who has won just one of his seven professional encounters with his compatriot, is coached by Tiafoe's former coach Wayne Ferreira.

Tiafoe believes both players will know exactly what to expect from each other heading into their last four clash.

"It's a guy who knows me pretty well in Wayne," Tiafoe said. "I expect some good serving and all the best from him. Happy where I've been mentally more than anything. This has been a great week."

Italy's Flavio Cobolli faces Frenchman Arthur Fils in the other men's semi-final, with the US Open beginning later this month, live on Sky Sports.

Watch the ATP and WTA Tours live on Sky Sports. The US Open is also live on Sky Sports from August 30. Stream tennis with NOW.

articles.title: Alcaraz y Serena, 46 'Grand Slam' juntos en el mixto del US Open
articles.standfirst: Se confirma la pareja estrella del torneo junto a la que forman Djokovic y Sabalenka
articles.summary: Se confirma la pareja estrella del torneo junto a la que forman Djokovic y Sabalenka
articles.body: El nuevo US Open mixto, en la segunda edición que se programa la semana previa al inicio de los cuadros individuales, contará con una pareja que seguro llenará las gradas de la central Arthur Ashe, el estadio de tenis más grande del mundo con capacidad para más de 23.000 aficionados.  Lo que era un secreto a voces se ha confirmado oficialmente y Carlos Alcaraz y Serena Williams, separados por 22 años, se juntarán en un dúo histórico que suma 46 títulos del Grand Slam. Serena cuenta con 39 (23 individuales, 14 dobles y dos en mixtos) por los siete del fenómeno de El Palmar.  Los dos triunfos en mixtos de la leyenda estadounidense fueron con el bielorruso Max Mirnyi, en Wimbledon y el Abierto de los Estados Unidos, en 1998. Mirnyi es en la actualidad uno de los entrenadores de Sabalenka, número uno del circuito femenino.  Los otros dos grandes nombres que formarán juntos son Novak Djokovic (24 'majors') y Aryna Sabalenka, con seis grandes en su palmarés, entre individuales (4) y dobles (2).  Otros participantes destacados son Alexander Zverev y Taylor Townsend; Felix Auger-Aliassime y Alexandra Eala; Iga Swiatek al lado de Casper Ruud; o Flavio Cobolli con Belinda Bencic.  El cuadro principal estará compuesto por un total de 16 equipos y se disputará los días 25 y 26, con rondas de eliminación directa a partir de octavos. Los partidos son al mejor de tres sets (cuatro juegos por set) y un súper 'tie break' en caso de tener que acudir al desempate.  El lunes 24 se jugará la fase previa del certamen con ocho dúos y dos billetes en juego para unirse a los 14 clasificados directamente. Alcaraz y Serena, que no estaban apuntados en la lista inicial, han recibido una de las tres invitaciones de la organización. Carlitos participó en la edición de 2025 junto a Emma Raducanu. Cedieron en el debut ante Jessica Pegula y Jack Draper.  Dentro de la cifra récord en premios del US Open 2026, que se eleva a 108 millones de dólares, un millón irá destinados a la pareja campeona del atractivo mixto. Sólo por participar son 40.000 dólares. Los cuartos valen 120.000; las semifinales 250.000 y los finalistas se embolsarán medio millón a repartir.  Alcaraz volverá a competir de manera oficial 133 días después de la lesión en la muñeca derecha, que se produjo en su debut en el Barcelona Open Banc Sabadell con el finlandés Otto Virtanen.

articles.title: ¿Cuánto dinero se llevarían Alcaraz y Serena si ganan el mixto del US Open?
articles.standfirst: La bolsa en premios para los vencedores es de un millón de dólares a repartir
articles.summary: La bolsa en premios para los vencedores es de un millón de dólares a repartir
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz y Serena Williams serán una de las 16 parejas que disputará a partir del martes 25 de agosto la prueba del mixto del US Open. Con la mirada puesta en la competición individual, el murciano se lo toma como un banco de pruebas en una oportunidad histórica de jugar al lado de una leyenda de la raqueta como Serena.  Además de la diversión que supondrá ver en pista a Carlitos y la pequeña de las Williams, con el show asegurado, habrá una bolsa en premios que asciende a un millón de dólares para el dúo vencedor del certamen.  Sólo por participar son 40.000 dólares. Los cuartos valen 120.000; las semifinales 250.000 y los finalistas se embolsarán medio millón a repartir. Cabe recordar que la dirección del último grande ha anunciado un aumento del 20 por ciento respecto al año pasado en la dotación económica. Se alcanza una cifra récord de 108 millones de dólares a repartir entre todas las competiciones.  Ese aumento del 20 por ciento en las ganancias es lo que piden los profesionales de la raqueta al resto de Grand Slam, dígase Open de Australia, Roland Garros y Wimbledon. Tanto en París como en Londres, los tenistas protestaron a su manera y sólo atendieron a los medios por espacio de 15 minutos.

articles.summary: La estadounidense también se impuso ese año en el Wimbledon de la modalidad con la misma pareja
articles.body: Serena Williams, que el próximo 26 de septiembre cumplirá 45 años, buscará su segundo título en el dobles mixto del US Open, esta vez al lado de Carlos Alcaraz. La leyenda estadounidense ya inscribió su nombre en el palmarés en la edición de 1998, cuando apenas tenía 16 años.  Su acompañante era el bielorruso Max Mirnyi, con el que ya había triunfado meses antes sobre la hierba de Wimbledon. Mirnyi es en la actualidad uno de los entrenadores de Aryna Sabalenka, la número uno del circuito femenino. El técnico principal de Sabalenka es Anton Dubrov. En un cuadro de 32 parejas, Serena y Max vencieron en las semifinales a Debbie Graham y Sandon Stolle y en la final a los locales Lisa Raymond y Patrick Galbraith, por un doble 6-2.

articles.title: Serena Williams, Carlos Alcaraz Get Wild Card Into US Open Mixed Doubles Tournament in Return
articles.summary: Serena Williams is returning to the U.S. Open for the first time since 2022 as part of a marquee mixed doubles pair with Carlos Alcaraz.
articles.body:
Serena Williams is returning to the U.S. Open for the first time since 2022 as part of a marquee mixed doubles pair with Carlos Alcaraz.

The U.S. Open announced on Saturday that Williams and Alcaraz received one of the open wild-card entries to play mixed doubles starting Tuesday.

Williams was always careful to never use the word "retire" to explain her playing status. She did write in the August 2022 edition of Vogue , ahead of the U.S. Open, that she would be "evolving away from tennis" to focus on "other things that are important to me."

The 2022 U.S. Open had been the final tournament of Williams' career before playing doubles at the HSBC Championships in June. She has played in four tournaments primarily in doubles competition.

Williams' lone singles match since returning the court was at Wimbledon when she lost to Maya Joint in the first round. Her most recent appearance was on Monday in doubles action with her sister, Venus Williams, at the Cincinnati Open. They lost in three sets to Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns.

Alcaraz is also making his return to the court at the U.S. Open after a four-month absence due to a wrist injury. He announced on Thursday his participation in the final Grand Slam event of the year after missing the French Open and Wimbledon.

Since the mixed doubles tournament takes place before the singles competition, it allows Alcaraz the chance to get some playing time under his belt coming off a long layoff.

This will be Alcaraz's first time playing doubles since September 2025 when he was paired with Jakub Mensik in the Laver Cup.

The mixed doubles tournament will be played on Aug. 25 and 26.

articles.summary: Serena Williams to team up with Carlos Alcaraz for US Open mixed doubles tournament next week but American great will not be playing singles; watch the US Open from August 30 live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
The dream team of Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz have signed up to the US Open mixed doubles championship, but the American great won't be playing in the women's singles.

Williams will ‌make a competitive return to the ‌US Open alongside defending ​men's champion Alcaraz after ‌the pair were handed a ​wild card entry.

It will be ​Williams' first ⁠competitive match ⁠at Flushing Meadows since 2022 when she lost to Ajla Tomljanovic in the third round.

The American 23-time Grand Slam singles champion and ‌six-time US Open winner - who returned to tennis this summer - won the mixed doubles title in 1998 with ⁠Max Mirnyi.

Williams, who played singles at Wimbledon and doubles with older sister Venus at the Cincinnati Open, won't be playing singles in New York, after USTA handed their final women's wild card to Sofia Kenin.

Jamie Murray, speaking on Sky Sports Tennis, said: "Serena obviously hasn't played a singles match since Wimbledon but I don't know if she feels physically ready to get back on the singles court and compete or maybe she doesn't feel she can do that altogether.

"She's going to play some doubles with her sister Venus and she's got a fun event in the mixed doubles. I personally expected to see her across the US Open Series after Wimbledon - to play more matches with a view to competing in New York but obviously that's not the case."

Alcaraz announced this week he would return to defend his singles title after being sidelined since April with a right wrist injury.

World No 1 Aryna Sabalenka ​will partner four-time US Open winner Novak Djokovic and Jessica ⁠Pegula will team up with fellow ⁠American Taylor Fritz following withdrawals by their previous teammates Jack Draper and Elena Rybakina, respectively.

The mixed doubles main draw begins Tuesday.

articles.title: Granollers y Zeballos se quedan a un súper 'tie break' de la final del Masters 1000 de Cincinnati
articles.standfirst: La pareja hispano-argentina cede ante el alemán Frantzen y el neerlandés Haase en el torneo que ganaron en 2021
articles.summary: La pareja hispano-argentina cede ante el alemán Frantzen y el neerlandés Haase en el torneo que ganaron en 2021
articles.body: Marcel Granollers y Horacio Zeballos, segundos cabezas de serie del cuadro, no podrán repetir título en el Masters 1000 de Cincinnati después de ganar en la edición de 2021. La pareja hispano-argentina ha cedido este sábado en las semifinales del torneo de Ohio a manos del alemán Constantin Frantzen y el neerlandés Robin Haase, por 6-3, 3-6 y 10-5, en 1 hora y 17 minutos.  Granollers y Zeballos viajan ahora a Nueva York para intentar revalidar el título del US Open, uno de los tres Grand Slam que figuran en su palmarés junto a las dos últimas ediciones de Roland Garros.  Marcel era el último representante español en el TMS de Cincinnati tras la eliminación de Rafa Jódar en los octavos de individuales frente a Flavio Cobolli.

articles.title: Cincinnati Open: Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula to meet in tournament's first all-American women's final in 56 years
articles.summary: Jessica Pegula topples defending champion Iga Swiatek in her semi-final; fellow American Frances Tiafoe also reaches men's final and faces France's Arthur Fils; watch the US Open from August 30 live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Open will host its first all-American women's final in 56 years after Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula won their respective semi-finals.

Fourth seed Gauff cruised home in her clash with Sara Bejlek, eclipsing the Czech 6-4 6-1, while third seed Pegula earned her spot by toppling defending champion Iga Swiatek 7-5 4-6 6-4.

The last Cincinnati Open final to feature two American women came in 1970 when Rosie Casals defeated Nancy Richey.

Fellow American Frances Tiafoe also reached the men's final, where he will face France's Arthur Fils.

  • Latest tennis scores and results 🎾
  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW📱

Pegula dethrones Swiatek to secure Gauff final

Pegula rallied from a break down in the deciding ‌set to defeat six-time Grand Slam champion Swiatek in her semi-final.

World No 3 Pegula and seventh seed Swiatek traded breaks early in ​the opening set before rain briefly interrupted play with the score level at 1-1.

Swiatek ‌clawed her way back, breaking to level at 4-4 before moving ahead, but with the set locked at 5-5, Pegula capitalised ​on a Swiatek double fault to break for 6-5 before the Pole sent the simplest of smashes into the net to hand Pegula the opener.

In the second set, Swiatek was more aggressive, breaking in the ⁠sixth game to take a 4-2 lead.

Pegula broke back and managed to level the contest, but the former world No 1 levelled things up when Pegula missed a forehand return.

Pegula refused to fade after Swiatek moved 3-1 ahead in the decider. The American levelled at 4-4, earned the decisive break in the ‌next game and then served out for a memorable victory.

"It was a really tough match. She (Swiatek) is in great form. To beat someone who is such a great athlete like Iga in the semis and to make it to another 1000 final, it's ⁠awesome," Pegula said.

She will face Gauff in the final after the two-time Grand Slam winner made light work of unseeded Czech ​Bejlek in the last four.

The 20-year-old had stunned world No 1 Aryna Sabalenka and Madison Keys en route to booking her first WTA 1000 semi-final spot.

Gauff proved superior in the opening set, earning a 4-1 lead after breaking serve early on.

However, Bejlek managed to stay in contention and level at 4-4. It wouldn't be enough to stop the 22-year-old, however, who broke serve again before closing out the set.

Gauff then broke twice more in the second set, capitalising on a catalogue of Bejlek unforced ​errors to seal victory in 76 minutes.

Impressive Fils faces Tiafoe in men's final

Frenchman Fils produced a commanding ‌67-minute display to sweep aside seventh seed Flavio Cobolli ‌6-3 6-4 on Saturday and secure his ​place in the men's final in Cincinnati.

The 21st seed recovered ​quickly after Cobolli broke for ‌a 2-1 lead, breaking straight back to level ​at 2-2.

With the opening set locked at 3-3, Fils improved his performance ​to take a 4-3 lead ⁠before breaking decisively ⁠in the eighth game as Cobolli misfired from the ‌baseline.

Fils, who won the Barcelona Open in April, maintained his momentum in the ‌second set, breaking serve in the opening game.

Cobolli held to love at 4-3 to keep the pressure on but ⁠Fils proved superior, dictating play ​with sharp forehands to ​gain a 5-4 lead and ultimately ​clinch victory, having scored 22 winners ⁠and six aces.

"I was very happy with the performance," Fils said. "I started pretty slow. I was a bit tight, but I think from 4-3 in the first set when I won those long rallies, just the momentum came my way and I felt so much better."

Fils has risen 10 spots to No 11 in the ATP live rankings as a result of his run to the final, where he will face Tiafoe after he beat fellow American ​Brandon Nakashima 7-5 6-3 in their semi-final..

The pair traded four consecutive breaks before drawing level at 3-3 in the opening set, ​but Tiafoe held to love in the seventh game and broke again to move 6-5 ahead before serving out the set.

The 27-year-old broke Nakashima for a 3-2 lead in the second set ‌and would go on to clinch victory with another impressive hold to love.

She will face Gauff in the final after the two-time Grand Slam winner made light work of unseeded Czech ​Bejlek in the last four.

The 20-year-old had stunned world No 1 Aryna Sabalenka and Madison Keys en route to booking her first WTA 1000 semi-final spot.

Gauff proved superior in the opening set, earning a 4-1 lead after breaking serve early on.

However, Bejlek managed to stay in contention and level at 4-4. It wouldn't be enough to stop the 22-year-old, however, who broke serve again before closing out the set.

Gauff then broke twice more in the second set, capitalising on a catalogue of Bejlek unforced ​errors to seal victory in 76 minutes.

Impressive Fils faces Tiafoe in men's final

Frenchman Fils produced a commanding ‌67-minute display to sweep aside seventh seed Flavio Cobolli ‌6-3 6-4 on Saturday and secure his ​place in the men's final in Cincinnati.

The 21st seed recovered ​quickly after Cobolli broke for ‌a 2-1 lead, breaking straight back to level ​at 2-2.

With the opening set locked at 3-3, Fils improved his performance ​to take a 4-3 lead ⁠before breaking decisively ⁠in the eighth game as Cobolli misfired from the ‌baseline.

Fils, who won the Barcelona Open in April, maintained his momentum in the ‌second set, breaking serve in the opening game.

Cobolli held to love at 4-3 to keep the pressure on but ⁠Fils proved superior, dictating play ​with sharp forehands to ​gain a 5-4 lead and ultimately ​clinch victory, having scored 22 winners ⁠and six aces.

"I was very happy with the performance," Fils said. "I started pretty slow. I was a bit tight, but I think from 4-3 in the first set when I won those long rallies, just the momentum came my way and I felt so much better."

Fils has risen 10 spots to No 11 in the ATP live rankings as a result of his run to the final, where he will face Tiafoe after he beat fellow American ​Brandon Nakashima 7-5 6-3 in their semi-final..

The pair traded four consecutive breaks before drawing level at 3-3 in the opening set, ​but Tiafoe held to love in the seventh game and broke again to move 6-5 ahead before serving out the set.

The 27-year-old broke Nakashima for a 3-2 lead in the second set ‌and would go on to clinch victory with another impressive hold to love.

articles.standfirst: El US Open pondrá en juego el cetro de Sabalenka con cuatro aspirantes a liderar el circuito femenino
articles.summary: El US Open pondrá en juego el cetro de Sabalenka con cuatro aspirantes a liderar el circuito femenino
articles.body: El torneo de Cincinnati ha vuelto a poner de manifiesto que los tenistas estadounidense son mucho más competitivos en casa que fuera de sus fronteras. Frances Tiafoe se ha colado en la final masculina, que le enfrentará al francés Arthur Fils.  Por su parte, la prueba individual femenina tendrá una campeona de casa. Se medirán Coco Gauff y Jessica Pegula. El duelo entre ambas ha propiciado que las dos tengan opciones matemáticas de ascender al número uno de la WTA en la próxima edición del US Open (30 de agosto al 13 de septiembre).  Y es que Sabalenka, líder del circuito, no podrá sumar en las pistas de Flushing Meadows como vigente campeona. Como máximo, defenderá los 2.000 puntos del último título.  Rybakina es la que más cerca está de la bielorrusa. Les separan escasamente 434 puntos. De hecho, la kazaja pudo salir líder de Cincinnati en caso de alcanzar la final. Pero se retiró en los cuartos con Iga Swiatek a causa de una lesión en la rodilla.  Elena, Gauff y Pegula aspiran a convertirse en la trigésima jugadora que llega a la cima desde la introducción del ranking femenino.

articles.standfirst: El triunfo del francés en las semifinales de Cincinnati evitó que Nole cayera al sexto puesto del ranking
articles.summary: El triunfo del francés en las semifinales de Cincinnati evitó que Nole cayera al sexto puesto del ranking
articles.body: Novak Djokovic, que se ejercitó el sábado por primera vez en las pistas de Flushing Meadows, será el cuarto cabeza de serie en el cuadro que se sorteará el próximo jueves 27 de agosto. La victoria de Arthur Fils ante Flavio Cobolli, en las semifinales del Masters 1000 de Cincinnati, benefició al serbio, que no caerá así al sexto puesto de la clasificación mundial.  La ausencia de Jannik Sinner en Nueva York convierte a Djokovic en el cuarto favorito. Eso significa que sólo podría cruzarse con Alexander Zverev y Carlos Alcaraz, cabezas de cartel, en unas hipotéticas semifinales.  Novak persigue su vigésimo quinto grande, que le permitiría desempatar el récord de 24 que comparte con la australiana Margaret Court. Su último gran entorchado fue precisamente en la Arthur Ashe neoyorquina en la edición de 2023.  Fils, verdugo en Cincinnati de Cobolli, por 6-3 y 6-4, se jugará este domingo la corona con el local Frances Tiafoe, que acabó con la resistencia de Brandon Nakashima, por 7-5 y 6-3.

articles.title: Las reglas del mixto del US Open: sets de cuatro juegos, punto de oro, súper 'tie break' para desempatar...
articles.standfirst: El formato del innovador torneo, la semana previa a los cuadros individuales, fomenta el espectáculo
articles.summary: El formato del innovador torneo, la semana previa a los cuadros individuales, fomenta el espectáculo
articles.body: La organización del US Open ha convertido el último Grand Slam en un torneo de tres semanas. Después de lograr que la competición gane un día y empiece en domingo, como Roland Garros y el Open de Australia, ahora han convertido la semana de los aficionados en una gran fiesta.  Además de la tradicional fase previa, en las pistas del Billie Jean King Tennis Center, concretamente en las dos pistas principales, la Arthur Ashe y la Louis Armstrong, se celebrará los días 25 y 26 de agosto la segunda edición del revolucionario mixto del Abierto de los Estados Unidos.  Para fomentar la participación de las grandes figuras se adelantan las fechas y se reduce el torneo a dos días y 16 equipos. Se aumenta la bolsa en premios hasta el millón de dólares para el campeón.  El formato es lo más atractivo posible para el público, con partidos al mejor de tres sets (sets a cuatro juegos como las Next Gen Finals); punto de oro en iguales y súper 'tie break' a 10 puntos en caso de empate a una manga.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz ya se entrena en las pistas del US Open
articles.standfirst: El murciano aterrizó el sábado en Nueva York y este domingo realizó su primera práctica
articles.summary: El murciano aterrizó el sábado en Nueva York y este domingo realizó su primera práctica
articles.body: N o hay tiempo que perder para Carlos Alcaraz. El campeón de siete grandes, que viajó la mañana del sábado a Nueva York, desde Madrid, ya se ejercita este domingo en las pistas de Flushing Meadows para preparar su regreso a la competición oficial. Lo ha hecho practicando al lado de Samuel López y Álvaro Alcaraz.  Cuando salte a jugar el dobles mixto al lado de Serena Williams, el próximo martes 25 de agosto, habrán pasado 133 días desde la lesión en la muñeca derecha en la primera ronda del Barcelona Open Banc Sabadell.  Carlitos practicó este domingo en la cancha Louis Armstrong, la segunda en importancia del Billie Jean King Tennis Center, por detrás de la Arthur Ashe. La última vez que el tenista de El Palmar pisó la instalación fue el 7 de septiembre de 2025 cuando se impuso en la final a Jannik Sinner.  En la sesión, utilizó siempre una gorra ante los gritos de admiración de cientos de aficionados que no se quisieron perder los primeros golpes de Alcaraz en la ciudad de los rascacielos.  El murciano ha salido del túnel de vestuarios seguido por Juanjo López, su médico y que ha estado atento a todos los movimientos del tenista en pista.

articles.title: La semana de Roger Federer: vuelta a las pistas en Nueva York e ingreso en el Salón Internacional de la Fama
articles.standfirst: El suizo disputará un partido de individuales y otro de dobles en la semana previa al torneo
articles.summary: El suizo disputará un partido de individuales y otro de dobles en la semana previa al torneo
articles.body: Flushing Meadows volverá a disfrutar de Roger Federer en una pista de tenis. El campeón de 20 Grand Slam regresará a Nueva York para formar parte de la 'fan week' previa al cuadro principal del US Open.  El evento contará con la presencia de Roger Federer, Andy Roddick, John McEnroe y Andre Agassi, cuatro campeones de Grand Slam. La organización ha anunciado la disputa de un partido de individuales entre el suizo y Roddick a un set, sin ventajas. Y un segundo encuentro de dobles (Federer y McEnroe ante Roddick y Agassi) con el mismo formato. Todo esto sucederá el sábado 29 de agosto, un día antes del inicio de los cuadros masculino y femenino. Será una semana movida para el que fuera número uno del ranking ATP durante 310 semanas, ya que también se celebrará su ingreso en el Salón Internacional de la Fama. Será parte de la promoción de 2026 y el acto tendrá lugar en Newport del 27 al 29 de agosto. La leyenda suiza cuenta con 103 títulos en su haber, únicamente superado por el estadounidense Jimmy Connors (109). Roger Federer ha levantado el título de campeón del US Open hasta en cinco ocasiones, el que más junto a Jimmy Connors y Pete Sampras. Aunque con un aspecto distintivo, ya que es el único tenista en la historia que ha logrado defender la corona del último grande del año (2004-2008). La racha la cortó el argentino Juan Martín del Potro derrotando precisamente al suizo en la final en 2009.

articles.title: La 'Armada' acude con 15 tenistas a la fase previa del US Open
articles.standfirst: Nueve hombres y seis mujeres empiezan este lunes la búsqueda de un billete para el cuadro principal
articles.summary: Nueve hombres y seis mujeres empiezan este lunes la búsqueda de un billete para el cuadro principal
articles.body: En mitad del torneo mixto del US Open, con la gran expectación que ha despertado la dupla formada por Carlos Alcaraz y Serena Williams, y el regreso de Roger Federer a Flushing Meadows para disputar una exhibición con Andy Roddick, Andre Agassi y John McEnroe, se celebrará la fase previa del último 'major' (24 al 27). Un total de 15 miembros de la 'Armada', nueve hombres y seis mujeres, empiezan este lunes su andadura sobre el cemento de Nueva York.  En el cuadro masculino figuran Pedro Martínez, Roberto Carballés, Max Alcalá, Dani Rincón, Nikolas Sánchez Izquierdo, David Jordà, Pol Martín, Alejandro Moro y Pablo Llamas.  En categoría femenina buscarán el billete al cuadro principal Marina Bassols, Sara Sorribes, Leyre Romero, Angela Fita, Andrea Lázaro y Guiomar Maristany. Pedro Martínez, actualmente en el puesto 151 del ranking, ha recibido la confianza del seleccionador nacional David Ferrer y está entre los cinco convocados para la serie de Copa Davis en tierras chilenas los días 19 y 20 de septiembre.

articles.title: Cincinnati Open: Arthur Fils defeats Frances Tiafoe in historic ATP Masters 1000 final between two Black players
articles.summary: Young Frenchman Arthur Fils defeats home favourite Frances Tiafoe to win the Cincinnati Open; watch the US Open from August 30 live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Frenchman Arthur Fils may have played himself into contention to win the US Open after sealing the biggest title of his career at the Cincinnati Open on Sunday.

The 21st seed, who won the Barcelona Open in April, added the Cincy crown to his growing list of achievements with a topsy-turvy 6-3 1-6 6-0 victory over Frances Tiafoe in Ohio.

Fils became the third Black man to win a Masters 1000 title, joining Ben Shelton, who won the Canadian Open twice, and Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, who won Paris in 2008 and Canada in 2014.

"That feels good," said Fils, who dominated the deciding set to end France's 12-year wait for a Masters 1000 title. "There's a lot of training, a lot of sacrifice. Injury. To be able to win a title like this, it means a lot to me.

"I don't have any words to describe this. It feels so good. A little bit of relief as well."

Fils made a flying start by breaking early to establish a 3-0 ​lead in the opening set before ‌Tiafoe got on the board with a hold of serve.

The ​Frenchman maintained relentless pressure from the baseline, attacking Tiafoe's second serve and forcing errors as he moved ​5-3 ahead. Fils was untouchable on ⁠serve, closing out the ⁠set with three successive aces without dropping a point in the final ‌game.

Tiafoe, playing in his second Cincinnati final, responded in kind in the second set.

The 28-year-old broke in ‌the second game en route to a 3-0 lead, with his forehands pulling Fils wide. Although Fils got on the board with a hold to ⁠love, the 17th seed Tiafoe broke ​again for a 5-1 advantage before forcing ​a decider.

Fils quickly regained control in ​the third set, breaking twice to race into ⁠a 4-0 lead as Tiafoe's backhand errors piled up.

The 22-year-old's pace and movement proved too much ⁠for the American, and he ​closed out the match with a bagel ​final set after a lengthy rally to lift the trophy.

Tale of the Tape

Now 32-10 for the year, Fils is up eight spots to fifth in the ATP Live Race To Turin as a result of his run.

'Fils is like a ballet dancer'

Annabel Croft, speaking on Sky Sports Tennis:

"He talked about the sacrifices he made and the injuries he has had but what a performance that was in the final set. He played flawless tennis in the first set but he regrouped so well in that final set and breath-taking movement to watch him courtside.

"He's so agile, he's like a ballet dancer, and we saw every kind of shot that he could possibly come up with to win this title and to take on a home crowd as well it was really impressive."

Croft added: "He's so mature on the court. He's physically very mature and that was the aspect for me just how well this guy moves across the court. It's very dynamic. It's the take-off speed but it's also the agility. He can be on the front foot and attacking, but when he's pushed defensively he can turn on a sixpence and then put in the slices and defend so well."

"That feels good," said Fils, who dominated the deciding set to end France's 12-year wait for a Masters 1000 title. "There's a lot of training, a lot of sacrifice. Injury. To be able to win a title like this, it means a lot to me.

"I don't have any words to describe this. It feels so good. A little bit of relief as well."

Fils made a flying start by breaking early to establish a 3-0 ​lead in the opening set before ‌Tiafoe got on the board with a hold of serve.

The ​Frenchman maintained relentless pressure from the baseline, attacking Tiafoe's second serve and forcing errors as he moved ​5-3 ahead. Fils was untouchable on ⁠serve, closing out the ⁠set with three successive aces without dropping a point in the final ‌game.

Tiafoe, playing in his second Cincinnati final, responded in kind in the second set.

The 28-year-old broke in ‌the second game en route to a 3-0 lead, with his forehands pulling Fils wide. Although Fils got on the board with a hold to ⁠love, the 17th seed Tiafoe broke ​again for a 5-1 advantage before forcing ​a decider.

Fils quickly regained control in ​the third set, breaking twice to race into ⁠a 4-0 lead as Tiafoe's backhand errors piled up.

The 22-year-old's pace and movement proved too much ⁠for the American, and he ​closed out the match with a bagel ​final set after a lengthy rally to lift the trophy.

Tale of the Tape

Now 32-10 for the year, Fils is up eight spots to fifth in the ATP Live Race To Turin as a result of his run.

'Fils is like a ballet dancer'

Annabel Croft, speaking on Sky Sports Tennis:

"He talked about the sacrifices he made and the injuries he has had but what a performance that was in the final set. He played flawless tennis in the first set but he regrouped so well in that final set and breath-taking movement to watch him courtside.

"He's so agile, he's like a ballet dancer, and we saw every kind of shot that he could possibly come up with to win this title and to take on a home crowd as well it was really impressive."

Croft added: "He's so mature on the court. He's physically very mature and that was the aspect for me just how well this guy moves across the court. It's very dynamic. It's the take-off speed but it's also the agility. He can be on the front foot and attacking, but when he's pushed defensively he can turn on a sixpence and then put in the slices and defend so well."
