articles.title: Cincinnati Open: Coco Gauff beats Jessica Pegula in straight sets to clinch second Cincinnati title
articles.summary: In the first all-American women's final in Cincinnati for 56 years, Coco Gauff cruised to a 6-2 6-4 victory over Jessica Pegula; watch the US Open from August 30 live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Coco Gauff defeated fellow American Jessica Pegula in straight sets, 6-2 6-4, to capture her second Cincinnati Open women's singles title.

It means the world No 4 becomes just the third player in the Open Era, after Serena Williams and Victoria Azarenka, to win multiple titles in Cincinnati.

Pegula had beaten defending champion Iga Swiatek in the semi-finals, while Gauff disposed of unseeded Sara Bejlek - who had knocked out world No 1 Aryna Sabalenka - to set up the first all-American women's final in Cincinnati for 56 years.

  • Latest tennis scores and results 🎾
  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW📱

Gauff stormed out to a 5-0 lead in the first set, taking it 6-2. Pegula battled back to 5-4 in the second before Gauff, who converted five out of six break points in the contest, closed out the win.

"I think it was a long journey, but I'm happy," Gauff said. "I think it's night and day, the player I was last year to now.

"I don't think that this is an indicator that I'm going to do well in New York [at the US Open]. Just knowing the quality wins that I had this week, hopefully I can use that experience."

Gauff had five wins in straight sets in Cincinnati.

"I thought she just played at a really high level and didn't really have many dips," Pegula said. "I didn't really think I played bad.

"The more you construct the point [against her], the worse it is because she almost likes to run. It was tough today. A dangerous, confident Coco is going to New York."

The head-to-head series between Gauff and Pegula is now tied at five apiece. Sunday was their second meeting in a final, with Gauff winning at Wuhan last year.

articles.title: US Open Tennis: Alex Eala is the biggest thing to come out of the Philippines since legendary boxer Manny Pacquiao
articles.summary: Alex Eala achieved a big milestone by claiming the Washington Open but what are her chances in New York? Watch the US Open from August 30 live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
"Once it grows, it cannot be stopped" - tennis superstar-in-the-making Alex Eala is quickly becoming the biggest thing to come out of the Philippines since legendary boxer Manny Pacquiao.

The 21-year-old is carrying the hopes of a nation, the volume of support when she plays calling to mind the days when world boxing champion 'Pac Man' put the country on the map as a sporting force.

Few young players on the WTA Tour have experienced the level of expectation and support Eala has received ‌since she earned a place on the circuit, and she showed what all the fuss is about ‌by winning the recent Washington Open.

  • Latest tennis scores and results 🎾
  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract 📱

After a run to the fourth round of Wimbledon, which included a victory over defending champion Iga Swiatek, Eala capped her breakthrough in the US capital by rallying to defeat top seed Jessica Pegula 4-6 ​6-4 6-0 in a rain-interrupted final, becoming the first woman from her country to claim a tour-level singles crown.

Along the way, ​she beat Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen, last year's winner Leylah ‌Fernandez, second seed Elina Svitolina and four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka.

Her remarkable run of victories mark her down out as a ​dangerous outsider for the US Open, starting August 30 - live on Sky Sports.

"It's an incredible milestone for me," said Eala, who moved to Spain to attend the Rafa Nadal Academy on a scholarship at the age of 13. "Coming into the tournament, I knew that the competition was super strong and my draw was quite tough. Every match was a ‌different set of obstacles. I'm really proud.

"I ended the tournament in better shape than I started. Each match I kept improving and kept learning things about myself. So it definitely gives me ‌a lot of confidence.

"It's really nice to see all the things I've been working on off court or during training being implemented in matches."

Rise of the Filipino superstar-in-waiting

Eala's progress has been closely watched since her US Open junior triumph in 2022, and she reached the Eastbourne final last year before making the fourth ⁠round at Wimbledon - signalling a steady improvement.

As Eala's reputation grew, so ​too did her following, with large groups of Filipino fans packing ​the stands at tournaments around the world to back a player many see ​as a pioneer for tennis in their country.

Her popularity - like Pacquiao in his heyday - was evident in the final ⁠of the WTA 500 event in Washington. By the time the tournament ended, the phrase written across the Nike T-shirt she had worn earlier that week had become a reality: "Once it grows, it cannot be stopped."

Philippines president Ferdinand Marcos released a message on social media congratulating Eala on "yet another historic achievement", adding: "You continue to redefine what is possible for Philippine tennis and inspire countless young Filipinos to dream without limits."

The Philippines' sporting interests have historically been all about basketball, billiards and boxing, but the nation is now being swept up in tennis fever.

'Eala is class with a awkward lefty serve'

Sky Sports analyst Annabel Croft believes Eala can be one of the "biggest stars" and is "just what the tour needs" following her success in Washington.

The former British No 1 said: "I've never seen anything like it. The stadium, you could not get a seat. The noise, the excitement levels, and she just takes it all in her stride. And you could see in Washington what she brings to the court and she plays with such grace.

"There's a certain class about her. I love her attitude. I love the way she goes after the ball. She's a very deceptive tennis player. Being a lefty, she's quite awkward, but that forehand it's not a huge strike, but it does damage."

Croft has likened Eala's serve to that of former Wimbledon champion Angelique Kerber who relied heavily on her left-handed spin, placement, and variation.

She said: "I would imagine that she has built up some kind of locker-room respect right now where you build a certain aura and then that counts for quite a lot on the tour as well because players don't want to face you because of the record that she's building up.

"There's something awkward about a lefty serve, a little bit like Kerber. I remember she didn't have a big serve, but it was so well placed into the court. But also when you put a lot of spin on it and it sometimes has less pace on it, you're forcing your opponents to generate pace and they start to get a bit jittery.

"She keeps notching up the big wins, but she's also backing up the pressure wins.

"She plays under a lot of pressure with all of that excitement from the Filipino community. They turn out in their droves to watch her. That for some people would be a pressure, but she embraces it. She loves it."

Is Eala a US Open contender?

Asked whether Eala could be a contender at the US Open, Croft said: "She's obviously somebody who enjoys being on a big stage. There will be a lot of players that won't want to face her because she's very in form. And I think the hard courts really suit her game."

Eala partnered American tennis legend Venus Williams in the doubles in Toronto this month, resuming their pairing from the Bad Homburg Open in Germany earlier this year.

Williams had high praise for Eala, saying: "Alex is a world star. She's just incredible. Besides the fact of her tennis, she's an incredible person, well spoken, and just an impressive young lady."

Meanwhile, four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka has thanked Eala for bringing the Filipino community to tennis.

"I think it's great," said the Japanese star. "I finished my match and the little go-kart was taking me back. I looked at the practice court and it was completely full. I was like, 'who's practising right now?' She didn't even go on court yet and then I saw the Filipino flags and I was like, 'um-hum'.

"I think it's awesome. It's so cool that she's building a new community and obviously great for the tournament, because she sells a lot of tickets."

Watch the ATP and WTA Tours live on Sky Sports. The US Open is also live on Sky Sports from August 30. Stream tennis with NOW and the Sky Sports App.

articles.title: Los aficionados pagan la subida en los premios del US Open: 323 dólares la entrada más barata
articles.standfirst: El torneo empieza el domingo para ganar un día más de venta de abonos como el Open de Australia y Roland Garros
articles.summary: El torneo empieza el domingo para ganar un día más de venta de abonos como el Open de Australia y Roland Garros
articles.body: Los tenistas hacía tiempo que reclaman un mayor pastel en el reparto total de beneficios en los torneos del Grand Slam y el US Open ha sido el primero que ha dado un paso adelante para contentar a los profesionales de la raqueta. La dirección del certamen neoyorquino anunció el pasado jueves una cifra récord en premios que asciende a 108 millones de dólares. Eso significa un 20 por ciento más de dinero para los jugadores respecto a la pasada edición. Los campeones individuales, sin ir más lejos, se llevarán a casa un talón de cinco millones y medio de dólares. Carlitos ya ingresó en 2025 el mayor botín de la historia del tenis y que ascendió a cinco millones de dólares, que en euros fueron 4.291.770 euros. Craig Tiley, el dirigente que ha hecho más grande el Open de Australia, desembarca como máximo responsable de la USTA (Federación Americana de Tenis).  El organismo que explota los derechos del último grande del calendario ha puesto unos precios muy elevados para los aficionados que quieran asistir a partir de esta semana a las pistas de Flushing Meadows.  El martes se inicia oficialmente el torneo con el mixto. Una entrada en la Arthur Ashe va desde los 70 dólares hasta los casi 500. Esa misma jornada se celebra un partido de exhibición con Roger Federer como cabeza de cartel. En la central más grande del mundo, con capacidad para más de 23.000 espectadores, se venden los abonos entre 84 dólares y casi 900. Aunque lo más impactante es que para un abono en la primera jornada del cuadro individual, del domingo 30 de agosto -sólo con derecho a las canchas exteriores-, dispara su precio hasta los 323 dólares. Cada día de competición hay sesión de día y de noche, con tickets diferentes en función del horario.  Por el mismo día y el mismo tipo de billete, el Open de Australia cobró a sus seguidores 35 dólares. En Roland Garros la cifra fue de 45 dólares y en Wimbledon, considerado la catedral del tenis, fueron 44 dólares los que tuvieron que desembolsar los aficionados.  Millonarios tendrán que ser los que quieran ver de cerca la final femenina, con abonos de 1.696 dólares. Hasta 2.938 se dispara el ticket más caro para la final masculina.

articles.title: US Open Tennis Mixed Doubles Teams, Bracket, Prize Money and TV Schedule
articles.summary: The second year of the US Open's reformatted mixed doubles is set to kickoff on Tuesday and will feature plenty of top talent.
articles.body:
The second year of the US Open's reformatted mixed doubles is set to kickoff on Tuesday and will feature plenty of top talent.

The event, which is just two days, will offer fans a glimpse at some of the top players before the singles tournament gets underway next week.

Agassi, Serena and more iconic US Open outfits

Click on the post below to see the full bracket.

There's more than just bragging rights at stake: The winning duo will take home a $1 million prize, higher than most prize purses for mixed doubles major tournaments.

The tournament will feature 16 teams competing across two action-packed days.

On Tuesday, both the first round and the quarterfinals will be held, followed by the semifinals and the highly anticipated championship match on Wednesday night.

Matches will follow a best-of-three format, similar to standard doubles events. However, due to the tight schedule, only four games are needed to win a set—except for the championship match, which uses the traditional format.

If a match goes to a third set, a 10-point tie-breaker will determine the winner.

Additionally, no advantage scoring will be used, making each deuce point a thrilling, winner-takes-all moment.

Top seeds Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic will face Leylah Fernandez and American crowd favorite Frances Tiafoe in a blockbuster first-round matchup.

Fans will also get to see other headliners such as 23-time Grand Slam singles champion Serena Williams teaming up with Carlos Alcaraz.

There are three exciting all-American duos: Amanda Anisimova and Learner Tien, Jessica Pegula and Taylor Fritz, and Emma Navarro and Tommy Paul.

Meanwhile, Gael Monfils and Elina Svitolina will take the court as a husband-wife team.

Sara Errani and Andrea Vassavori will be looking to defend their title, though the exceptionally talented field promises fierce competition.

Sara Errani and Andrea Vassavori will be looking to defend their title, though the exceptionally talented field promises fierce competition.

articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz aterrizó el sábado en Nueva York para preparar el US Open, evento en el aparece en el cuadro individual y también en el del mixto. En esa modalidad formará una histórica dupla con Serena Williams. Entre los dos se reparten 46 títulos del Grand Slam.  Alcaraz participó en la pasada edición del mixto, en el Abierto de los Estados Unidos, al lado de la británica Emma Raducanu. Cedieron a manos de Jack Draper y Jessica Pegula.  Serena, por su parte, ya sabe lo que es ganar el US Open mixto. Lo hizo en 1998 junto al bielorruso Max Mirnyi, actual entrenador de Aryna Sabalenka. El partido de octavos de Alcaraz y Serena, contra Erin Routliffe y Lloyd Glasspool, será el martes 25 de agosto en la central Arthur Ashe. El  duelo está fijado no antes de las 14.00 horas en Nueva York, que son las 20.00 horas en España.    El partido de Carlos Alcaraz y Serena Williams, de los octavos de la prueba mixta del Abierto de los Estados Unidos, se podrá ver en Movistar+. La última hora y todo lo que ocurra en el encuentro a través de MARCA.com y Radio MARCA.

articles.standfirst: El murciano ha completado el segundo entrenamiento en Flushing Meadows, antesala del debut en el mixto
articles.summary: El murciano ha completado el segundo entrenamiento en Flushing Meadows, antesala del debut en el mixto
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha completado este lunes su segundo entrenamiento en las pistas de Flushing Meadows. A diferencia del domingo, donde tuvo su primera toma de contacto en la Louis Armstrong, esta vez ha sido en la Arthur Ashe, la majestuosa central del barrio de Queen's donde ganó la pasada campaña su segundo título.  Alcaraz, que el domingo práctico con su hermano Álvaro y con Samuel López, se ha ejercitado durante una hora al lado de su compatriota Dani Mérida.  Los dos tenistas españoles realizaron un calentamiento de media hora en una de las pistas exteriores y posteriormente se desplazaron a la pista principal. Allí jugaron un set que más bien pareció un partido oficial. El campeón de siete grandes siempre juega pegado a la malla que luce en su brazo derecho desde que regresó a las prácticas en Murcia una vez anunció su renuncia al Masters 1000 de Cincinnati.  La elección de Mérida para la sesión no es casualidad. El madrileño, el 39 del ranking, es uno de los jugadores más en forma del circuito. Sus buenos resultados le han valido para entrar en la convocatoria de España en la serie de Copa Davis ante Chile los días 19 y 20 de septiembre.

articles.standfirst: Un total de 15 españoles aparecen en los cuadros de la fase clasificatoria
articles.summary: Un total de 15 españoles aparecen en los cuadros de la fase clasificatoria
articles.body: El tenis español ha empezado con mal pie su andadura este lunes por la fase previa del US Open, el último grande del curso que se celebra en las pistas de Flushing Meadows. Roberto Carballés, el 209 del ranking ATP a sus 33 años, ha caído a manos del británico Jacob Fearnely, por 7-6(3) y 6-3. También se despidió Alejandro Moro ante el suizo Remy Bertola, 6-3 y 6-4.  Dani Rincón, flamante campeón junior del torneo neoyorquino en 2021, remontó al galo Titoan Droguet, 2-6, 6-4 y 7-6(1). Tampoco pudo pasar la criba inicial el catalán Pol Martín, apeado por Tom Gentzsch, por 7-5 y 6-3.  En el cuadro femenino, Andrea Lázaro dio buena cuenta de la armenia Elina Avanesyan, por 6-3 y 7-6(3). Angela Fita también se impuso a la china Lin Zhu, por 6-4 y 7-6(7).

articles.title: Roger Federer returns to play US Open exhibition match, live on Sky Sports - but has no interest in professional comeback
articles.summary: Roger Federer will return to play at Flushing Meadows for the first time since 2019, as the five-time US Open champion features in an exhibition event; watch Roger Federer: An Icon Returns to New York live on Sky Sports Main Event on Wednesday morning at 1am BST
articles.body:
Roger Federer is set to make a long-anticipated return to play at Flushing Meadows as the five-time consecutive US Open men's singles champion will play in an exhibition match, live on Sky Sports.

The 45-year-old will walk out onto the court at Arthur Ashe Stadium as a player for the first time since he was beaten by Grigor Dimitrov in 2019.

After a knee injury prevented him from entering the draw for the 2020 US Open, Federer would not return to play at the Grand Slam before announcing his retirement in September 2022.

  • Follow all the US Open build-up LIVE!
  • Latest tennis scores and results 🎾
  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract 📱

The Swiss tennis great never got his opportunity to say a proper farewell to the New York fans during his playing career.

But he will get his chance with his exhibition match, Roger Federer: An Icon Returns to New York, set to be broadcast live on Sky Sports Main Event from 1am (BST) on Wednesday morning.

"It really gives me a true opportunity to say thank you and goodbye, which I think is important for some," Federer said.

"It's a nice thing to do, for sure."

Federer will play one set of singles against Andy Roddick before he teams up with John McEnroe to face off against Roddick and Andre Agassi in a doubles match as part of the exhibition event.

However, the 20-time Grand Slam champion said he was nervous about the event.

"It's nerve-wracking. I haven't played a singles set in, I don't know, since [Hubert] Hurkacz at Wimbledon in 2021 maybe, so it's been five years," Federer said on Monday, referring to the final Grand Slam match of his career.

"I don't know how it's going to go tomorrow. There is a lot of uncertainty but a lot of happiness that I can return to Arthur Ashe, a place where I have had so many beautiful memories."

Serena Williams' surprise partnership with Carlos Alcaraz for the mixed doubles event has been the talk of the tournament.

But when asked if he'd consider coming out of retirement like Williams, aged 44, Federer responded: "No, not at all.

"Thanks for asking. I wasn't sure if the question was going to get asked, but I'm happy you did so I can clarify in case anybody thought."

articles.title: Inspiring story of the day: âI almost died after giving birth to my daughter.â - How Serena Williams turned life-threatening motherhood and family strength into sporting resilience
articles.summary: International Sports News: Serena Williamsâ story of motherhood is also a story of survival. In 2017, the tennis star won the Australian Open while eight weeks pregnant, then ne.
articles.body: Serena Williamsâ story of motherhood is also a story of survival. In 2017, the tennis star won the Australian Open while eight weeks pregnant, then nearly died after giving birth to her daughter, Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr. An emergency C-section was followed by a pulmonary embolism, more surgery and six weeks in bed. Serena later returned to the highest level of tennis, reaching four straight Grand Slam finals. Her daughter Olympia became an important part of that journey. Years later, Serena chose to step away from singles tennis to focus on her family, while continuing to build her life beyond the court.How did Serena Williams almost die after giving birth to Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr.Serenaâs pregnancy had gone well, but the birth of Olympia on September 1, 2017, quickly became dangerous. Olympia was delivered by emergency C-section after her heart rate dropped sharply during contractions. The surgery itself went well, and Serena was able to hold her daughter. The serious problems started about a day later.Serena suddenly had trouble breathing. Because she had a history of blood clots, she suspected she was having another pulmonary embolism, a condition in which a blood clot blocks blood flow in the lungs. She asked for a CT scan and blood thinner treatment. Doctors later found several small clots in her lungs.The treatment then caused another problem. Serenaâs intense coughing made her C-section wound open. Doctors found a large hematoma, or a collection of blood, in her abdomen. She needed more surgery and another procedure to help stop future clots from reaching her lungs. After leaving the hospital, Serena spent the first six weeks of motherhood in bed and had difficulty even walking.Serena later described the experience in a CNN opinion piece, making clear just how close she believed she had come to losing her life.âI almost died after giving birth to my daughter, Olympia. Yet I consider myself fortunateâ¦ When I finally made it home to my family, with only days left in my recovery, I felt a deep sense of gratitude just to hold my baby girl in my arms.âThe CNN piece was also about the wider problem of maternal health and the need for better access to care. Serena credited the doctors and nurses who treated her with helping save her life.How did Alexis Ohanian support Serena Williams during her recoveryFor Serena, recovering from childbirth was not only about getting her body strong enough to play tennis again. She was also learning how to care for a newborn while she was unable to move normally.Her husband, Alexis Ohanian, was there during that difficult period. In Serenaâs 2018 Vogue interview, Ohanian spoke about how hard it was to watch his wife struggle while he could not take away what she was going through. Serena also described how difficult those first weeks were as a new mother.That made her return to tennis different from any comeback she had made before. She was not simply trying to get her ranking back. She was trying to find a way to be a professional athlete and a mother at the same time.When Serena returned to competition, she faced another challenge. After her long break, she had fallen far down the rankings and had to work her way back into major events. She eventually reached the 2018 Wimbledon final, less than a year after giving birth.How did Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr. become Serena Williamsâ motivationOlympia was born into a world where her mother was already one of the biggest names in tennis. But after the difficult birth, motherhood gave Serena a different reason to keep going.During her return, Serena spoke openly about the emotional side of being a mother and an athlete. Her run to the Wimbledon final in 2018 became one of the clearest signs that she could still compete at the highest level after everything her body had gone through.After the Wimbledon final, Serena also dedicated her performance to mothers watching her. She had lost to Angelique Kerber, but the result did not take away from what she had achieved by reaching the final so soon after giving birth.âOlympia, does mama look good out here? Youâre the reason Iâm here, youâre my motivation. To all the moms out there, I was playing for you today. Itâs okay to have hard days, but we keep fighting.âThat message summed up what her comeback had come to mean. Serena was not hiding the difficult parts of motherhood. She was showing that returning to work after having a child can involve fear, setbacks and days when the body simply does not cooperate.Her run did not stop at Wimbledon. Serena reached four straight Grand Slam singles finals after becoming a mother: Wimbledon and the US Open in 2018, followed by the Australian Open and Wimbledon in 2019. She did not win those finals, but reaching them showed how quickly she had returned to the top of the sport.Why did Serena Williams choose family when she stepped away from tennisBy 2022, Serena was ready for another major change. She did not want to call it retirement. In her Vogue essay announcing her decision to move away from professional tennis, she called it an âevolution.âHer decision was closely tied to her family. Serena wrote about Olympiaâs wish to become a big sister and her own desire to have another child. At the same time, she wanted to give more attention to Serena Ventures and the other parts of her life that had grown alongside her tennis career.âI have never liked the word retirementâ¦ Maybe the best word to describe what Iâm up to is evolution. Iâm here to tell you that Iâm evolving away from tennis, toward other things that are important to meâ¦ My daughter wants to be a big sister, and I want to be there for my family.âVogue published Serenaâs essay in August 2022, ahead of what she described as her final US Open. She later welcomed her second daughter, Adira River Ohanian, with Alexis Ohanian in August 2023.Serenaâs tennis story has since taken another unexpected turn. In 2026, she returned to competitive tennis, making her comeback first in doubles and later joining Carlos Alcaraz for the US Open mixed doubles event. That means her relationship with the sport is still evolving, even after she stepped away from singles competition in 2022.Her motherhood journey remains one of the most personal parts of that story. Serena went from a frightening medical crisis after Olympiaâs birth to competing in Grand Slam finals again. She then made a choice to put family at the centre of her next chapter. For Serena, strength was not only about winning another match. It was also about surviving, recovering and finding a new reason to keep moving forward.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: âLet sport decide, not a spreadsheet.â That was the sharp message from twotime Asian Games gold medallist Rohan Bopannaas the pruning of Indiaâs tennis squad by the sports ministry for the Aichi-Nagoya Games triggered a fresh debate over selection policy.Bopanna backed five players who have been dropped from the 12-member list recommended by the All India Tennis Association (AITA), questioning the wisdom of deciding medal prospects before players have stepped on to the court.âIf outcomes are already decided, why have qualifications at all? Why rankings?â he wrote on social media.The ministry-approved seven-member tennis contingent comprises Sumit Nagal and Dhakshineswar Suresh for menâs singles; Yuki Bhambri, N Sriram Balaji and Anirudh Chandrasekar for menâs doubles and Ankita Raina and Rutuja Bhosale for womenâs doubles.There is no womenâs singles representation.Importantly, the 2026 Asiad singles champions can earn an ITF quota place for the LA 2028 Games, subject to eligibility requirements. Not sending a singles specialist could hurt the nationâs Olympics chances.The omissions are Manas Dhamne, Vaishnavi Adkar, Sahaja Yamalapalli, Vaidehee Chaudhari and Prarthana Thombare.The ministry, however, has shown no inclination to revisit its decision.TOIsent a detailed questionnaire to the ministry, Sports Authority of India and TOPS division seeking a formal response to the Bopanna-led criticism. articles.body: Roger Federer is in New York this week, but not to compete. The 45-year-old Swiss legend is headlining "Roger Federer: An Icon Returns to New York," an exhibition during US Open Fan Week at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Tuesday, August 25. With Serena Williams making an actual competitive return at this year's tournament, the obvious question found its way to Federer at a pre-event press conference: could he do the same? His answer was emphatic, and it left zero room for interpretation.Does Roger Federer have any plans to make an official tennis comeback?None. Not even close. When asked whether he could envision making an official return similar to what Serena Williams has done this year, Federer did not hesitate."No, no, no, no, no, not at all. Thanks for asking. I wasn't sure if the question was going to get asked, but I'm happy you did so I can clarify in case anybody thought so. No, no, no, not at all. And I think you anyway have to enter the doping pool; like, God, there are way too many obstacles," he said.He then went further, essentially closing the door on any lingering fantasy. "And I'm too busy. I'm barely finding time to play any exhos. So imagine a Tour and the body is done. But I'm very happy how I'm feeling. So, all good and just a fan now. Just enjoying watching."Both Federer and Serena Williams retired in September 2022. Serena chose the US Open as her farewell. Federer played his final match alongside Rafael Nadal at the Laver Cup. Their paths since retirement, though, have been very different. Williams returned to competitive play in June, competed in doubles on grass, and accepted a singles wildcard at Wimbledon, where she lost in three sets before withdrawing with an injury. She and Venus eventually reunited at the Cincinnati Open last week, falling in their opening match.Federer is not interested in any of that. His last official singles match was actually at the 2021 Wimbledon Championships, a quarterfinal loss to Hubert Hurkacz, more than a year before his formal farewell. And he says he has not missed the grind one bit.What has Roger Federer been doing since retiring from professional tennis?More tennis, just on his own terms. He has been training in the gym, hitting with his wife, spending time with his kids, and occasionally sharing a court with current players. On Monday, he trained with Lorenzo Musetti ahead of the exhibition."I've been in the gym a lot. I love working out with my wife and with my friends whenever we hang out. So I've been doing a lot of that. It's not like playing tennis, and when you haven't played, you get an unbelievable amount of muscle pain. So, I feel my body's ready for tomorrow, but again, we're not playing best of five," Federer said.âVery quickly when youâre retired, you go through days and weeks and months all of a sudden where youâre hitting very little. So, you have to make it a priority. And my kids are getting older, so I get a chance to play more with them. And depending on where we are.âThe exhibition itself is a proper nostalgia event. Federer will play a one-set shootout against Andy Roddick, then team up with John McEnroe for a doubles match against Roddick and Andre Agassi. It will also be his first time back at Flushing Meadows since his 2019 US Open appearance, a tournament he won five consecutive times between 2004 and 2008, still the last man to defend the title there.Four days after the exhibition, Federer will be inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in Newport, Rhode Island, on August 29.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ¿Quiénes son Erin Routliffe y Lloyd Glasspool, los números uno rivales de Alcaraz y Serena en el US Open?
articles.standfirst: Los especialistas en dobles pasaron brillantemente la fase previa del torneo neoyorquino
articles.summary: Los especialistas en dobles pasaron brillantemente la fase previa del torneo neoyorquino
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz y Serena Williams ya conocen sus rivales en los octavos del US Open, que se celebrarán esta tarde a partir de las 20.00 horas en España, seis horas menos en Nueva York. Los primeros adversarios del dúo de leyendas serán Erin Routliffe y Lloyd Glasspool. La neozelandesa y el británico son dos consumados especialistas a mitad de pista, como lo demuestra su ranking.  Routliffe, de 31 años, es actualmente la decimocuarta raqueta de dobles en el circuito WTA y llegó a ser la primera en julio de 2024. En su palmarés figuran 13 títulos, el más reciente fue este verano en Washington. Es doble campeona del Abierto de los Estados Unidos en dobles, en 2023 y 2025.  Por su parte, Glasspool, de 32 años, es el decimoséptimo de las listas y fue número uno en agosto de la pasada campaña. En sus vitrinas aparecen 14 torneos ganados, entre ellos Wimbledon 2025. En el presente curso se impuso en Barcelona y en Washington al lado de su habitual pareja, el también británico Julian Cash.  Se ganaron el billete para el cuadro final del mixto desde la previa, con sendas victorias en dos súper 'tie break' ante Luisa Stefani y Neil Skupski y Kristina Mladenovic y Marcelo Arévalo.  La checa Katerina Siniakova y el británico Henry Patten son el otro dúo que superó la fase clasificatoria. Ahora toparán con los primeros cabezas de serie, Novak Djokovic y Aryna Sabalenka.

articles.title: Albacete tendrá una Copa Davis de leyendas: Italia contra España
articles.standfirst: Ferrer y Robredo jugarán por la selección nacional mientras que Cecchinato y Seppi lo harán por Italia
articles.summary: Ferrer y Robredo jugarán por la selección nacional mientras que Cecchinato y Seppi lo harán por Italia
articles.body: España e Italia, los dos grandes dominadores del tenis en la actualidad, gracias a nombres como Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner, Rafa Jódar o Flavio Cobolli, vivirán un particular duelo de Copa Davis los días 26 y 27 de septiembre en la IV Copa de Leyendas del Tenis Albacete.  Para conmemorar el 25º aniversario de la eliminatoria de la máxima competición por países ante Uzbekistán, celebrada en el club, se ha organizado una confrontación de leyendas entre España e Italia.  Por la selección nacional jugarán David Ferrer, el actual capitán de la 'Armada', y Tommy Robredo, que es el director del Barcelona Open Banc Sabadell, precisamente en sustitución de Ferru.  El combinado italiano estará formado por Marco Cecchinato y Andreas Seppi. El formato será de dos partidos de individuales y un dobles, en caso de que sea necesario para desempatar.  Ferrer estará una semana antes en Santiago de Chile donde la 'Armada' de 2026 se juega a domicilio uno de los siete billetes para la Final a 8 de la Copa Davis de Bolonia (24 al 29 de noviembre).

articles.title: Vondrousova appeals against four-year ban for refusing anti-doping test
articles.summary: Former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova did not let an anti-doping official enter her home to carry out a test in December 2025 and her ban is set to run until June 2030.
articles.body:
Former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova has appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) against her four-year ban for refusing an anti-doping test.

The 27-year-old was handed the ban in June after the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) charged her with denying a doping control officer entry to her home to conduct an out-of-competition test in December 2025.

Her suspension is due to end on 21 June 2030.

Cas confirmed to BBC Sport that it had received the appeal but said a hearing date had not yet been set.

Vondrousova, who in 2023 became the first unseeded player to win the Wimbledon women's singles title, said in April that when she refused the test she was at "breaking point after months of physical and mental stress".

The Czech added that she feared for her safety when the officer called at her home at 20:00 on 3 December and said they failed to properly identify themselves or follow "protocol". She signed a refusal form when she went outside to walk her dog shortly afterwards.

However, a tribunal determined Vondrousova provided "no compelling justification" for refusing the test, nor to receive a shortened ban.

Mental stress led to anti-doping charge - Vondrousova Published 17 April

Mental stress led to anti-doping charge - Vondrousova

Dog walk and expletive text - key findings in Vondrousova anti-doping case Published 31 July

Dog walk and expletive text - key findings in Vondrousova anti-doping case

Players are required to log their whereabouts for an allotted hour each day so authorities can conduct anti-doping tests outside of competition.

Vondrousova, a former French Open finalist and Olympic silver medallist, wrote in a statement following her ban: "I have never doped, I have never had a positive test. Throughout my entire career I have undergone countless anti-doping controls and have always stepped on the court with a clear conscience."

The former world number six hasn't played since reaching the second round of the Adelaide International in January and has slipped down to 153rd in the WTA rankings.

articles.title: Ranking the 10 Best US Open Tennis Outfits of All Time
articles.summary: The 2026 U.S. Open gets underway on Sunday, and you know what that means: It's time to show off some 'fits.
articles.body:
The 2026 U.S. Open gets underway on Sunday, and you know what that means: It's time to show off some 'fits.

Whether you're in the stands or on the court, the U.S. Open has become synonymous with bold fashion choices.

Style has become an essential component of the U.S. Open experience, and seeing the players express themselves through their kits is one of the many highlights of the next few weeks.

While the popularity of U.S. Open fashion seems to grow every year, it's not new. Tennis stars have been breaking boundaries and pushing the limits with their attire at the event since its inception in 1895.

As we look forward to all of the bold outfits to come, let's look back at the 10 best U.S. Open outfits of all time.

Famous for his penchant for bold color schemes, Francis Tiafoe's 2023 U.S. Open getup is a standout among the hundreds of hues he's worn.

The teal backdrop against the pink, tan, and maroon print is an unexpected combination, but heck, it works.

The psychedelic vibes, combined with the texture's functionality, make it all feel oddly practical, but maybe that's just Tiafoe's confidence doing the talking. He's in Nike here, but his recent partnership with Lululemon is the perfect match for a man who favors bold prints juxtaposed with functional textures.

At the 1999 U.S. Open, Venus and Serena Williams famously wore feed-in braids with beads as they took the court. Venus wore all-white beads, while Serena matched with white beads and a distinct two-strand pink accent in the back.

They often wore their hair in braids early in their careers as a nod to their roots and a celebration and acknowledgment of their culture. It was awesome to see two young stars come onto the scene and absolutely dominate a sport long notorious for its lack of diversity. From the beginning, Venus and Serena were authentic, unapologetic forces shaping every facet of the game.

Osaka's 2025 U.S. Open look gave us one of the best headlines in tennis history, courtesy of People magazine : Naomi Osaka Wears Crystal-Embellished U.S. Open Outfit Featuring a Bedazzled Labubu Named 'Billie Jean Bling'

Was all of this completely absurd? Of course. Did it all somehow still work?

Osaka has never been afraid to take fashion risks, and it's put her on the tennis fashion radar for good. At the 2025 U.S. Open, she donned a red Nike jacket over a matching Nike tennis dress with a bubble skirt. She had sparkly roses in her hair, and yes, she had a matching, crystal-embellished Labubu as an accessory.

Much like Andre Agassi and his mullet in 1988 and Serena Williams and her denim skirt in 2004, the U.S. Open is a great reflection of fashion trends of the time. Perhaps unfortunately, Labubus were huge in 2024 and 2025. It was cool to see Osaka put her own twist on a trend.

Coco Gauff was a few years ahead of her time at the 2023 U.S. Open. Burgundy and chartreuse have become one of the trendiest color combinations of 2026, especially in sneaker culture and activewear.

She debuted her extremely popular burgundy shoe with New Balance this year, and yes, this was the year she won the U.S. Open.

Sometimes, a simple fit with a slightly unusual but aesthetically pleasing colorway really gets the job done.

Williams was never one to shy away from a tutu, and this lilac dress from the 2018 U.S. Open is our favorite among all of her tutu looks.

The mock-neck tennis dress was a departure from her penchant for streetwear, and showed she can pull off just about any vibe. It may look like this dress had one shoulder, but the right shoulder blended in seamlessly with her skin by design, which is a fun feature.

The look was a highly anticipated collaboration between Nike and Off-White, and it lived up to the hype.

You may recall this fit came right after the controversy in which she wore a catsuit, which was later banned, at the French Open.

It was a statement: Williams was not going to stop getting creative with her outfits.

Maria Sharapova's 2006 U.S. Open dress remains one of the most iconic looks in tennis fashion history.

The dress itself was iconic enough on its own, inspired by Audrey Hepburn and adorned with Swarovski crystals. But Sharapova also became the first player to debut different day- and night-session match kits, switching into the dress for her night-session.

Sharapova was just 19 when she donned the dress, and it's become part of tennis lore, as she captured the 2006 U.S. Open wearing it.

Classy, revolutionary, and sparkly, this dress was the perfect foray into nighttime fashion at the Open.

A cheeky nod to Brat Summer, Osaka's bright green ensemble at the 2024 U.S. Open is one of many inventive looks from the star that have already elevated her to one of the best-dressed players of all time.

The look featured bows throughout, including on the back of her sneakers. There was also a removable green and white tulle tutu, and an accompanying white windbreaker with—you guessed it—a bow.

Osaka told the New York Times that she, Nike, and designer Yoon Ahn drew inspiration from Japanese fashion, especially for the bows.

"I remember one of the first times I went to Japan, I saw so many frills and so many bows," Osaka said . "I wouldn't automatically associate myself with being girlish when I'm on the court, but I tend to gravitate toward really beautiful and cute things. I think there's something quite cool in making that an emphasis."

Osaka has become the modern name to watch in tennis fashion for a reason.

When your outfit has a nickname that's been around for decades, that's either a really good or a really bad thing.

Roger Federer famously wore all black at the 2007 U.S. Open, and the stadium DJ played along by playing the Darth Vader Imperial March from Star Wars as he walked onto the court.

It was a big departure from Federer's typical lighter color palette, and it happened at the perfect time in the midst of one of his most memorable runs. At the end of the season, Federer became the only player in history to win three majors in a year for three years (2004, 2006, 2007).

Williams has so many looks to pick from, and her domination while wearing so many of these kits instantly makes them 10 times "tuffer," as the kids say.

Her 2004 Nike-designed denim look, featuring leather boots that deserve a spot in the tennis hall of fame, is the boldest in a sea of bold fashion choices for the legend.

This was a great blend of streetwear and functionality, especially considering 2004 was a peak year for streetwear in general.

Williams has referred to this look as her favorite she's ever donned, and in a Hot Ones interview, she said it was a nod to Agassi's denim moment in the 1988 U.S. Open (spoiler alert: We may see that one soon).

Tournament officials deemed the boots "too over the top" for gameplay, but Williams gets brownie points for at least attempting to push that boundary.

There were tennis icons making fashion statements before Andre Agassi ever took the court, of course. The early-to-mid 1900s saw barriers broken aplenty, like Suzanne Lenglen's calf-length, uncorseted dresses in the '20s and Gussie Moran's laced-trim knickers, which debuted in 1949.

Still, it's fair to say Agassi is the father of the evolution of on-court fashion. He did the most to revolutionize tennis style, opting for streetwear reflective of the '80s and '90s as opposed to the traditional, all-white country club attire.

His use of denim and spandex established new textures worn on the court that are still popular today. The 1988 U.S. Open featured arguably his most iconic fit, or kit if you want to call it that: The Jorts.

Agassi was one of the first players to ever appear on the U.S. Open court in denim shorts. The tiny, acid wash jorts were designed by Nike, and accompanied by a very late '80s mullet.

Look, we're not looking at this fit and calling acid wash jorts and a mullet the pinnacle of high fashion. This look is iconic because it represented rebellion, creativity, and the beginning of more streetwear-influenced tennis style.

They often wore their hair in braids early in their careers as a nod to their roots and a celebration and acknowledgment of their culture. It was awesome to see two young stars come onto the scene and absolutely dominate a sport long notorious for its lack of diversity. From the beginning, Venus and Serena were authentic, unapologetic forces shaping every facet of the game.

Osaka's 2025 U.S. Open look gave us one of the best headlines in tennis history, courtesy of People magazine : Naomi Osaka Wears Crystal-Embellished U.S. Open Outfit Featuring a Bedazzled Labubu Named 'Billie Jean Bling'
Was all of this completely absurd? Of course. Did it all somehow still work?

Osaka has never been afraid to take fashion risks, and it's put her on the tennis fashion radar for good. At the 2025 U.S. Open, she donned a red Nike jacket over a matching Nike tennis dress with a bubble skirt. She had sparkly roses in her hair, and yes, she had a matching, crystal-embellished Labubu as an accessory.

Much like Andre Agassi and his mullet in 1988 and Serena Williams and her denim skirt in 2004, the U.S. Open is a great reflection of fashion trends of the time. Perhaps unfortunately, Labubus were huge in 2024 and 2025. It was cool to see Osaka put her own twist on a trend.
Coco Gauff was a few years ahead of her time at the 2023 U.S. Open. Burgundy and chartreuse have become one of the trendiest color combinations of 2026, especially in sneaker culture and activewear.
She debuted her extremely popular burgundy shoe with New Balance this year, and yes, this was the year she won the U.S. Open.
Sometimes, a simple fit with a slightly unusual but aesthetically pleasing colorway really gets the job done.
Williams was never one to shy away from a tutu, and this lilac dress from the 2018 U.S. Open is our favorite among all of her tutu looks.

The mock-neck tennis dress was a departure from her penchant for streetwear, and showed she can pull off just about any vibe. It may look like this dress had one shoulder, but the right shoulder blended in seamlessly with her skin by design, which is a fun feature.
The look was a highly anticipated collaboration between Nike and Off-White, and it lived up to the hype.
You may recall this fit came right after the controversy in which she wore a catsuit, which was later banned, at the French Open.
It was a statement: Williams was not going to stop getting creative with her outfits.
Maria Sharapova's 2006 U.S. Open dress remains one of the most iconic looks in tennis fashion history.

The dress itself was iconic enough on its own, inspired by Audrey Hepburn and adorned with Swarovski crystals. But Sharapova also became the first player to debut different day- and night-session match kits, switching into the dress for her night-session.
Sharapova was just 19 when she donned the dress, and it's become part of tennis lore, as she captured the 2006 U.S. Open wearing it.
Classy, revolutionary, and sparkly, this dress was the perfect foray into nighttime fashion at the Open.

A cheeky nod to Brat Summer, Osaka's bright green ensemble at the 2024 U.S. Open is one of many inventive looks from the star that have already elevated her to one of the best-dressed players of all time.
The look featured bows throughout, including on the back of her sneakers. There was also a removable green and white tulle tutu, and an accompanying white windbreaker with—you guessed it—a bow.
Osaka told the New York Times that she, Nike, and designer Yoon Ahn drew inspiration from Japanese fashion, especially for the bows.

"I remember one of the first times I went to Japan, I saw so many frills and so many bows," Osaka said . "I wouldn't automatically associate myself with being girlish when I'm on the court, but I tend to gravitate toward really beautiful and cute things. I think there's something quite cool in making that an emphasis."
Osaka has become the modern name to watch in tennis fashion for a reason.
When your outfit has a nickname that's been around for decades, that's either a really good or a really bad thing.
Roger Federer famously wore all black at the 2007 U.S. Open, and the stadium DJ played along by playing the Darth Vader Imperial March from Star Wars as he walked onto the court.

It was a big departure from Federer's typical lighter color palette, and it happened at the perfect time in the midst of one of his most memorable runs. At the end of the season, Federer became the only player in history to win three majors in a year for three years (2004, 2006, 2007).
Williams has so many looks to pick from, and her domination while wearing so many of these kits instantly makes them 10 times "tuffer," as the kids say.
Her 2004 Nike-designed denim look, featuring leather boots that deserve a spot in the tennis hall of fame, is the boldest in a sea of bold fashion choices for the legend.
This was a great blend of streetwear and functionality, especially considering 2004 was a peak year for streetwear in general.

Williams has referred to this look as her favorite she's ever donned, and in a Hot Ones interview, she said it was a nod to Agassi's denim moment in the 1988 U.S. Open (spoiler alert: We may see that one soon).
Tournament officials deemed the boots "too over the top" for gameplay, but Williams gets brownie points for at least attempting to push that boundary.

There were tennis icons making fashion statements before Andre Agassi ever took the court, of course. The early-to-mid 1900s saw barriers broken aplenty, like Suzanne Lenglen's calf-length, uncorseted dresses in the '20s and Gussie Moran's laced-trim knickers, which debuted in 1949.

Still, it's fair to say Agassi is the father of the evolution of on-court fashion. He did the most to revolutionize tennis style, opting for streetwear reflective of the '80s and '90s as opposed to the traditional, all-white country club attire.

His use of denim and spandex established new textures worn on the court that are still popular today. The 1988 U.S. Open featured arguably his most iconic fit, or kit if you want to call it that: The Jorts.
Agassi was one of the first players to ever appear on the U.S. Open court in denim shorts. The tiny, acid wash jorts were designed by Nike, and accompanied by a very late '80s mullet.

Look, we're not looking at this fit and calling acid wash jorts and a mullet the pinnacle of high fashion. This look is iconic because it represented rebellion, creativity, and the beginning of more streetwear-influenced tennis style.

articles.title: Joao Fonseca dice adiós al US Open
articles.standfirst: El brasileño continúa con su recuperación del abdominal y no disputará el último grande del año
articles.summary: El brasileño continúa con su recuperación del abdominal y no disputará el último grande del año
articles.body: Tras las recientes bajas de Jannik Sinner y Jack Draper, el nombre de Joao Fonseca se une a la lista. El tenista brasileño continúa con la recuperación de la lesión abdominal y se ha visto obligado a bajarse del US Open 2026. “Hola a todos. Quería darles una actualización. Después de someterme a pruebas y empezar un tratamiento en el abdomen, nos ha quedado claro a mi equipo y a mí que necesito más tiempo para recuperarme y poder competir de nuevo al más alto nivel. Desafortunadamente, eso significa que no podré estar en el US Open. No ha sido una decisión fácil de tomar, ya que es un torneo muy especial para mí. Seguiremos trabajando para poder volver lo antes posible. Agradezco inmensamente todos los mensajes de apoyo y todas las felicitaciones de cumpleaños. ¡Muchas gracias!”, fue el mensaje que publicó el brasileño en sus redes sociales. Al igual que en el Masters 1000 de Cincinnati, donde tuvo que abandonar en la tercera ronda del torneo ante el australiano Christopher O'Connell, el abdomen no le da tregua al actual número 26 del mundo y terminará la gira americana de pista rápida con cuatro partidos disputados (tres en Montreal y uno en Ohio). De esta forma, Joao Fonseca se despide de los 'majors' esta temporada. Marcando su mejor resultado en la tierra de París siendo capaz de remontar un saco de dos sets a Novak Djokovic y logrando los cuartos de final. Ahí cedió ante el checo Jakub Mensik en tres mangas. El balance del brasileño en los tres Grand Slam disputados en 2026 es de seis victorias y tres derrotas.

articles.title: 'No, not at all': Roger Federer, 45, rules out return to professional tennis
articles.summary: Tennis News: Roger Federer has made it clear that fans should not expect to see him return to professional tennis.The 20-time Grand Slam champion, who retired in 2.
articles.body: Roger Federer has made it clear that fans should not expect to see him return to professional tennis.The 20-time Grand Slam champion, who retired in 2022, is set to play an exhibition match at the US Open but said his appearance in New York is purely for fun and not the start of a comeback.Asked whether he could return to the professional tour, Federer gave a straightforward response.âNo, not at all," Federer said at a press conference, according to Olympics.com.The Swiss great explained that making a comeback would require him to meet several professional obligations, including joining the anti-doping testing pool. More importantly, he said his busy schedule and physical condition make a return unrealistic.âThanks for asking. I wasn't sure if the question was going to get asked, but I'm happy you did, so I can clarify in case anybody thought. Anyway, you have to enter the doping pool. There are way too many obstacles. I'm too busy. I'm barely finding time to play any exhos [exhibition matches], so imagine a tour, and the body is done," Federer said.The 45-year-old added that he is comfortable with life away from competitive tennis and now enjoys watching the sport rather than playing it at the highest level.âBut I'm very happy with how I'm feeling. I'm just a fan now, enjoying watching," he added.A new chapter for the Swiss legendFederer last played at the US Open in 2019 before announcing his retirement three years later. He remains the only player, male or female, to win five consecutive US Open titles, achieving the feat from 2004 to 2008.His exhibition appearance comes shortly before another major milestone: his induction into the International Tennis Hall of Fame. Federer was selected in his first year of eligibility and will be inducted on August 29 in Newport, Rhode Island.The Swiss star won 20 Grand Slam singles titles, along with 103 tour-level trophies and Olympic gold and silver medals, before calling time on his legendary career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rafa Jódar vuelve al lugar donde empezó todo: de campeón del júnior del US Open a gran sensación del año
articles.standfirst: El madrileño, de 19 años, disputará por primera vez el grande neoyorquino como profesional
articles.summary: El madrileño, de 19 años, disputará por primera vez el grande neoyorquino como profesional
articles.body: Rafa Jódar cedió en los octavos del Masters 1000 de Cincinnati ante Flavio Cobolli y se tomó un descanso de tenis antes de aterrizar ayer en Nueva York. Este martes, tendrá su primera toma de contacto con las pistas de Flushing Meadows, las mismas que le vieron ganar hace dos temporadas en la prueba júnior del US Open.  Rafa disputará por primera el cuadro de los profesionales y lo hará con el cartel de decimosegundo cabeza de serie. El madrileño se ha convertido en la gran sensación de 2026 gracias a su salto en el ranking. Ha pasado del puesto 165 al 13.  Los registros de Jódar no dejan de asombrar. Se ha convertido en el mejor jugador de la Era Open tras la disputa de 50 partidos. Su balance es de 36 victorias por 14 derrotas. Sólo el argentino José Luis Clerc firmó esos números desde 1968.   Rafa mejora también las cifras del 'Big Three' y Carlos Alcaraz en sus inicios en los torneos Masters 1000, la segunda categoría del tenis después de los Grand Slam. Suma 15 triunfos en 20 partidos.  El tenista del Chamartín realizará hoy su primera sesión preparatoria en el Billie Jean King Tennis Center. Su acompañante será el ruso Karen Khachanov, el 49 de las listas ATP. El entreno está fijado a partir de las 14.30 horas en la ciudad de los rascacielos cuando más aprieta el sol.

articles.title: NYC Mayor Mamdani to Make 1,000 'Affordable' US Open Tickets Available to Local Residents
articles.summary: Amid concerns over the soaring ticket prices for the US Open, local fans in New York City have a new solution.
articles.body:
Amid concerns over the soaring ticket prices for the US Open, local fans in New York City have a new solution.

Per The Athletic's Adam Crafton , New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani has secured 1,000 "affordable" tickets for the tournament to distribute to local residents on a first-come, first-served basis.

Crafton reported that Mamdani will announce that $100 tickets will be available for New York City residents to purchase for main-draw matches taking place between Aug. 30 and Sept. 8, running through the quarterfinal stage of the tournament. Tickets will become available on Wednesday at 10 a.m. ET, and buyers must have a certified NYC zip code to be eligible.

"This summer, we have shown again and again that sports belong to the people. From the World Cup to track and field championships, we have opened stadium doors to some of the biggest sporting events in the world so more New Yorkers can enjoy them," Mamdani said in a statement to Crafton. "Today, we are doubling down on that work by making the US Open more affordable for New Yorkers. If the world's best tennis players are coming to our city, New Yorkers should be able to see them play."

It was noted that these particular tickets will not be eligible for resale through Ticketmaster, the tournament's secondary market platform. Ticketmaster has been the source of the price surge, with "grounds passes going for between $240 and $478 as of Tuesday morning, despite the face-value price for the cheapest being $65."

The tickets available for local residents will include ground passes and seats in Arthur Ashe Stadium and Louis Armstrong Stadium. The U.S. Open mixed doubles competition will be held on Tuesday and Wednesday, while the singles main draws will start on Sunday.

articles.title: US Open 2026: Stan Wawrinka thanks tournament after missing out on wildcard
articles.summary: Stan Wawrinka says his US Open triumph will "forever be one of the greatest moments of my life" after missing out on a wildcard for a farewell appearance in New York.
articles.body:
Stan Wawrinka says his US Open triumph will "forever be one of the greatest moments of my life" after missing out on a wildcard for a farewell appearance in New York.

The 41-year-old will retire at the end of year and was given a wildcard for this year's Australian Open and Wimbledon, while reaching the French Open main-draw on ranking.

He reached the third round in Melbourne and lost a pair of entertaining first-round matches in Paris and Wimbledon respectively.

The US Open has received some criticism for its decision not to award a wildcard to 2016 champion Wawrinka, who did not enter qualifying despite being inside the cut-off.

The United States Tennis Association (USTA) says it does not comment on wildcard decisions.

Despite not receiving a wildcard, Wawrinka thanked the US Open and the city of New York in a social media post.

"When I first arrived in New York from a small farming village in Switzerland, everything felt too big. The city. The noise. The energy. The crowds. The lights," the Swiss wrote.

"But, year after year, New York slowly became one of my favourite places in the world.

"This city challenged me. It pushed me. It brought something out of me that few places ever could.

"I experienced some of the strongest emotions of my career here. The battles, the late nights, the incredible atmosphere, the love from the crowdâ¦ memories that will stay with me forever.

"Winning the US Open, in the city that never sleeps, will forever be one of the greatest moments of my life."

Alcaraz and Williams thrill in US Open mixed doubles Published 59 minutes ago

Alcaraz and Williams thrill in US Open mixed doubles

GB's Dart and Jones advance in US Open qualifying Published 1 hour ago

GB's Dart and Jones advance in US Open qualifying

Wawrinka was one of the few players to win major singles trophies during the 'Big Three' era of Novak Djokovic, Rafael Nadal and Roger Federer.

The former world number three won the 2014 Australian Open and 2015 French Open before triumphing at the US Open 10 years ago.

He made 17 appearances in the men's singles in New York since making his main-draw debut in 2005.

Wawrinka's coach, Magnus Norman, wrote on Instagram: "We pushed to play one last Grand Slam at 41 years of age but we just came up short.

"It sure hurts but thanks for all the beautiful memories on and off the court together with you and the team in New York for the past 13 years."

Wildcards are given to players who did not qualify automatically for the tournament by ranking. Wawrinka has fallen outside the top 100 after struggling with injuries and form in recent years.

Switzerland also does not host a Grand Slam, with tournaments reserving reciprocal wildcards for one another.

France's Gael Monfils, who is also retiring this season, was given a wildcard through the French Tennis Federation, which organises the French Open.

Reciprocal wildcards are assigned by the national federations and not the US Open.

The US Open gets under way on Sunday, 30 August at Flushing Meadows.

Other than the reciprocal wildcards the USTA reserves for French and Australian players, the other six wildcards for both the men's and women's singles went to Americans.

The USTA organises and bankrolls the US Open, and would argue it has every right to put its own players first.

But when a charismatic champion like Wawrinka is not given the chance to say a proper farewell to the event he won in 2016, then the sport as a whole suffers.

Home players dominate the list of wildcards at all the Grand Slams, but the Australian Open found space for Stan Wawrinka and Venus Williams, while Wimbledon offered wildcards to Wawrinka, Grigor Dimitrov, Serena Williams and French Open runner-up Maja Chwalinska.

"It sure hurts but thanks for all the beautiful memories on and off the court together with you and the team in New York for the past 13 years."

Wildcards are given to players who did not qualify automatically for the tournament by ranking. Wawrinka has fallen outside the top 100 after struggling with injuries and form in recent years.

Switzerland also does not host a Grand Slam, with tournaments reserving reciprocal wildcards for one another.

France's Gael Monfils, who is also retiring this season, was given a wildcard through the French Tennis Federation, which organises the French Open.

Reciprocal wildcards are assigned by the national federations and not the US Open.

The US Open gets under way on Sunday, 30 August at Flushing Meadows.

Other than the reciprocal wildcards the USTA reserves for French and Australian players, the other six wildcards for both the men's and women's singles went to Americans.

The USTA organises and bankrolls the US Open, and would argue it has every right to put its own players first.

But when a charismatic champion like Wawrinka is not given the chance to say a proper farewell to the event he won in 2016, then the sport as a whole suffers.

Home players dominate the list of wildcards at all the Grand Slams, but the Australian Open found space for Stan Wawrinka and Venus Williams, while Wimbledon offered wildcards to Wawrinka, Grigor Dimitrov, Serena Williams and French Open runner-up Maja Chwalinska.

The 41-year-old will retire at the end of year and was given a wildcard for this year's Australian Open and Wimbledon, while reaching the French Open main-draw on ranking.
He reached the third round in Melbourne and lost a pair of entertaining first-round matches in Paris and Wimbledon respectively.
The US Open has received some criticism for its decision not to award a wildcard to 2016 champion Wawrinka, who did not enter qualifying despite being inside the cut-off.
The United States Tennis Association (USTA) says it does not comment on wildcard decisions.
Despite not receiving a wildcard, Wawrinka thanked the US Open and the city of New York in a social media post.
"When I first arrived in New York from a small farming village in Switzerland, everything felt too big. The city. The noise. The energy. The crowds. The lights," the Swiss wrote.
"But, year after year, New York slowly became one of my favourite places in the world.
"This city challenged me. It pushed me. It brought something out of me that few places ever could.
"I experienced some of the strongest emotions of my career here. The battles, the late nights, the incredible atmosphere, the love from the crowdâ¦ memories that will stay with me forever.
"Winning the US Open, in the city that never sleeps, will forever be one of the greatest moments of my life."

articles.title: Djokovic y Sabalenka duran 49 minutos en el mixto del US Open
articles.standfirst: Siniakova y Patten, los actuales números uno del dobles, remontan un set y ganan en el súper 'tie break'
articles.summary: Siniakova y Patten, los actuales números uno del dobles, remontan un set y ganan en el súper 'tie break'
articles.body: Novak Djokovic y Aryna Sabalenka, que se habían retado a bailar en las escaleras de Roland Garros, se juntaban este martes por primera vez en una pista de tenis para jugar el mixto del US Open. Los primeros cabezas de serie del cuadro, porque cuenta el ranking de individuales, tenían como rivales a los verdaderos números uno. Y es que Henry Patten y Katerina Siniakova son líderes en las respectivas clasificaciones masculina y femenina de dobles en el circuito ATP y WTA. Djokovic y Sabalenka cayeron con estrépito ante Siniakova y Patten, por 1-4, 4-2 y 10-2, en el súper 'tie break' que se alargó 49 minutos. En el deporte y en el tenis gana el que más quiere ganar. Para el serbio y la bielorrusa era una exhibición más, con media entrada en la Arthur Ashe. Para sus verdugos, una victoria que vale 120.000 dólares y que les acerca al botín de un millón. Sabalenka hace tiempo que piensa más en su indumentaria que en la raqueta. Volvió a lucir un colgante que no le aporta nada en el juego, más bien es una molestia.  De hecho, la tenista de Minsk no depende de ella para mantener el liderato de la WTA. Se lo arrebatará Elena Rybakina si alcanza las semifinales.  Siniakova y Patten cayeron después en la antepenúltima ronda con Gael Monfils y Elina Svitolina, por 5-4, 4-5 y 10-8, en 1 hora y 34 minutos. Y es que el galo y la ucraniana, que contrajeron matrimonio en 2021, quieren despedirse a lo grande. Monfils, de 39 años, cuelga la raqueta a finales de temporada.  En la Louis Armstrong, el segundo estadio del Billie Jean King Tennis Center, el dúo checo formado por Jakub Mensik y Karolina Muchova necesitó también de un súper 'tie break' para eliminar a Marcelo Arévalo y Kristina Mladenovic, por 4-1, 2-4 y 10-7. Después se colaron en las semifinales tras superar a los locales Emma Navarro y Tommy Paul, 4-1 y 5-3.

articles.title: Novak Djokovic, Aryna Sabalenka Lose in 1st Round of Mixed Doubles Bracket at 2026 US Open
articles.summary: One of the top pairs in the US Open mixed doubles competition is already out of the tournament.
articles.body:
One of the top pairs in the US Open mixed doubles competition is already out of the tournament.

No. 1-seeded Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka lost in the first round on Tuesday against the mixed doubles world No. 1 pair of Katerina Siniakova and Henry Patten, 1-4, 4-2, 10-2. Siniakova sent an ace past Djokovic for match point.

Agassi, Serena and more iconic US Open outfits

Djokovic and Sabalenka were originally slated to take on Frances Tiafoe and Leylah Fernandez. However, the lineup had to be shuffled after Tiafoe withdrew from the tournament on Monday due to injury, giving the No. 1 pair a tough test right out of the gate.

Early on, Djokovic and Sabalenka appeared to have the advantage as they cruised to a first-set victory, winning three straight points to close out the frame. After falling behind 2-1 in the second set, Patten and Siniakova stormed back to win the next three points and force a tiebreaker. The duo showed why they're No. 1 in the world with a dominant performance in the deciding set.

"It wasn't looking very good for a while," Patten said after the win, per The Athletic's Lukas Weese . "In this format, we played one game and the first set is gone. We played an amazing tiebreak. Kat acing Novak on match point was pretty fun."

Patten and Siniakova didn't have much time to rest before returning to action, as their second-round matchup against the married couple of Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils is already underway at Arthur Ashe Stadium.

articles.title: Asian Games tennis row deepens as AITA rebuts SAI's omission allegation
articles.summary: Tennis News: NEW DELHI: The row over India's tennis squad for the 2026 Asian Games intensified on Tuesday after the All India Tennis Association (AITA) categorical.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The row over India's tennis squad for the 2026 Asian Games intensified on Tuesday after the All India Tennis Association (AITA) categorically rejected claims that it failed to submit the names of excluded players to the Indian Olympic Association (IOA).The national federation denied a claim made by Sports Authority of India (SAI) source to news agency PTI that the omitted players â Manas Dhamne, Sahaja Yamalapalli, Vaishnavi Adkar, Vaidehee Chaudhari and Prarthana Thombare â did not feature in the shortlist forwarded by AITA to the IOA, and therefore were absent from the final list considered by the Sports Ministry.However, TimesofIndia.com has accessed the letter dated July 3 which was sent to the IOA CEO Raghuram Iyer where merits of each player, including recent history, was mentioned.AITA stated that Secretary General Sunder Iyer had written to Iyer on July 3, making an "urgent representation seeking review of the exclusion of tennis players from the Indian contingent" and specifically naming Dhamne, Ankita Raina, Yamalapalli, Chaudhari, Adkar and Thombare.In the four-page letter sent on July 3, accessed by TimesofIndia.com, AITA had argued that India should field its strongest possible contingent and maximise medal opportunities across all five tennis events rather than relying solely on uniform ranking criteria.On Monday, as TimesofIndia.com reported, the Sports Ministry had stuck by its selection policy, which requires singles players to be among Asia's top six and doubles players to be inside the continental top-eight over a 12-month evaluation period. The ministry has also maintained that the criteria will not be relaxed despite criticism made by two-time Asian Games medallist Rohan Bopanna.AITA's case for the quartetThe federation's representation highlighted that India had earned multiple strong acceptance-list positions in doubles events.AITA said India had three mixed doubles pairs inside the top-eight accepted entries â Rutuja Bhosale/Yuki Bhambri (seeded No. 2), Ankita Raina/N. Sriram Balaji (No. 5) and Prarthana Thombare/Anirudh Chandrasekar (No. 8). Since each country can enter only two pairs, AITA argued this represented two genuine medal opportunities.It also pointed out that Thombare and Bhosale were positioned at No. 10 on the women's doubles acceptance list, with withdrawals potentially opening the door to the main draw. Excluding established doubles specialists, the federation said, would weaken India's medal prospects.For the singles events, AITA described Yamalapalli as India's highest-ranked women's singles player, praised Adkar's international multi-sport credentials, backed Chaudhari's consistency on tour and termed 18-year-old Dhamne one of India's brightest young prospects whose Asian Games participation would aid both immediate competitiveness and long-term Olympic development.The letter concluded by requesting the IOA to urgently review the exclusions, reassess entries on an event-specific basis and approve all six players to maximise India's medal chances.Ministry steadfast in exclusionsThe controversy erupted after the exclusion of five players from the original 12 member list drew criticism from two-time Asian Games gold medallist Rohan Bopanna.Bopanna had said that "a committee that never stood where they stood has decided their fate on paper, before a ball is struck," adding that denying players the chance to compete was against the principles of building a sporting nation.The Ministry, however, has maintained that recent performances did not establish sufficient medal probability and argued that creating discretionary exceptions for players ranked between 25th and 40th in Asia would undermine administrative integrity and invite litigation from other national sports federations.India's final tennis squad currently includes Sumit Nagal in men's singles, while Yuki Bhambri, Dhakshineswar Suresh, N. Sriram Balaji, Anirudh Chandrasekar, Ankita Raina and Rutuja Bhosale have been selected for the doubles events.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz exit US Open mixed doubles in quarter-finals; top seeds Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka out in first round
articles.summary: Serena Williams, 44, wins her first match since 2022 after her return to tennis in June; mixed doubles defending champions Andrea Vavassori and Sara Errani out in first round; watch the 2026 US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Star pairing Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz reached the quarter-finals of the US Open mixed doubles before being beaten by fourth seeds Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli.

Williams - a 23-time Grand Slam singles champion - returned to tennis in June at the age of 44 and secured her first professional win since 2022 as she and Alcaraz beat Britain's Lloyd Glasspool and partner Erin Routliffe in their opening match.

It was also seven-time major winner Alcaraz's first match back on tour after a wrist injury sidelined the reigning men's singles champion since April. The 22-year-old was born five years after Williams won the 1998 mixed doubles title at Flushing Meadows.

  • Latest tennis scores and results 🎾
  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract 📱

The dynamic pairing bounced back from a slow start to claim a 5-3 4-1 opening victory over Routliffe and Glasspool, much to the delight of fans inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.

"I never expected to be back on this court," Williams said. "I never thought this would happen."

With their quarter-final match scheduled immediately afterwards, Williams and Alcaraz ultimately ran out of puff as Bencic and Cobolli triumphed 5-4 4-1, the latter then having hailed their opponents pre-match as "the queen of tennis and the king of now."

The question now is whether Williams will seek an encore performance in women's doubles alongside older sister Venus, having already ruled out a repeat of her singles appearance at Wimbledon.

Djokovic and Sabalenka suffer early exit

Top seeds Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka were bounced out of the tournament in the opening match on Arthur Ashe, falling to a 1-4 4-2 10-2 ‌defeat to Britain's Henry Patten and Katerina Siniakova.

Djokovic, a ​24-time Grand Slam singles champion, and four-time major winner Sabalenka made a strong start by ​taking the opening set, but doubles specialists Patten and ‌Siniakova hit back to claim the second before dominating the tiebreak ​to secure a place in the quarter-finals.

Siniakova sealed the upset in style with an ace out wide on match ​point, ending the tournament hopes of the ⁠star-studded pairing.

"It wasn't looking very ⁠good for a while, in this format we play one bad game and all ‌of a sudden the first set's gone," Patten said.

"We knew the same could happen in the second, and we played ‌an amazing tiebreak. Kat acing Novak on match point was great."

The mixed doubles championship is once again being staged in the week before the singles main draw, after organisers revamped ⁠the format last year to attract more ​leading singles players by reducing the field and ​giving the event a standalone slot on the ​calendar.

The revamped format proved a commercial success in its ⁠debut year, drawing sell-out crowds and attracting many of the sport's biggest singles names despite criticism from some doubles specialists, ⁠who argued it marginalised established pairings.

Defending champions dumped out in first round

Italian ​duo Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori went on to ​retain the title by defeating Iga Swiatek and Casper Ruud in last year's final, but suffered a first-round exit this year.

Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev beat the defending champions 1-4 4-1 11-9 in the opening round, before clinching a semi-final spot with a 4-1 4-5 10-5 victory over Diana Shnaider and Casper Ruud.

They next face Czech pair Karolína Muchova and Jakub Mensik in one of Wednesday's semi-finals, with Bencic and Cobolli facing husband and wife partnership Gael Monfils and Elina Svitolina in the other after they edged out Patten and Siniakova in the last eight.

The final two follow the two semis on Wednesday night will resemble a regular match, with traditional sets to six games.
